info.title: Netwrix Privilege Secure for Access Management API
info.description: REST API for Netwrix Privilege Secure for Access Management. Operations available in the web console are available through this API. Sign in to get a JSON Web Token (JWT) and send it in the Authorization header as a bearer token.

servers.description: Your Privilege Secure server. The console and the API use port 6500.

host.description: Host name or address of your Privilege Secure server.

get.summary: List access certification denials for an access policy
get.description:
Returns the access certification decisions recorded for one access policy, with the resource, credential, activity and task names filled in. By default it returns only decisions that have been resolved as approved or denied.

Permission required: Access Policies permission, and the Admin or UserPlus role.

Values for `[].status`: 0 = NotSet, 1 = Requested, 2 = Approved, 3 = Denied.

parameters.name: policyId
parameters.description: The ID of the access policy.

parameters.name: includeAll
parameters.description: Set to true to include decisions that are still pending. The default is false.

200.description: Returns an array of denials. The array is empty when the policy has none.

400.description: The denials could not be retrieved.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role or permission.

get.summary: List access certification denials for a user
get.description:
Returns the access certification decisions recorded for one managed user account.

Permission required: Any signed-in user.

Values for `[].status`: 0 = NotSet, 1 = Requested, 2 = Approved, 3 = Denied.

Caution: The response lists access certification decisions for the named account.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The ID of the managed user account.

200.description: Returns an array of denials. The array is empty when the user has none.

400.description: The denials could not be retrieved.

delete.description:
Deletes one denial that an access certification review recorded. Use it to remove a denial you no longer want to apply.

Permission required: Admin role.

Caution: The denial is deleted immediately and the call cannot be undone.

parameters.name: denialId
parameters.description: The ID of the denial to delete.

202.description: The delete was accepted. The body is the denial ID. The call also returns 202 when no denial has that ID.

400.description: The denial could not be deleted.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

get.summary: Export an access certification task as CSV
get.description:
Returns the task details followed by every activity row selected for the task, as comma-separated text. Commas inside values are replaced with spaces, and a pipe character (|) inside a value becomes a comma, which shifts the columns. Use it to export a task for reporting.

Permission required: Admin or Reviewer role.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The ID of the task to export.

200.description: Returns the CSV text as a JSON string.

400.description: The export failed.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The task does not exist.

put.summary: Submit a review for an access certification task
put.description:
Records the reviewer's approve or deny decisions for activity rows and sets the task status. When the status is Complete (3), the task is closed and each row's decision is recorded as a certification decision for that user's access.

Permission required: Reviewer role, and the signed-in user must be the task's reviewer.

Values for `summary.status`: 0 = Setup, 1 = ReadyToStart, 2 = Incomplete, 3 = Complete.

Values for `activitiesDetail[].status`: 0 = NotSet, 1 = Requested, 2 = Approved, 3 = Denied.

Caution: Setting the status to Complete closes the task and records its decisions immediately, and the task can no longer be reviewed. Sending 0 (Setup) or leaving the status out puts the task back into setup, so the reviewer can no longer see or review it.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The ID of the task being reviewed.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The status number to set on the task. Send 2 (Incomplete) while saving decisions, and 3 (Complete) to finish the review. Always send it: the server does not check which status you send, and if you leave it out it is treated as 0 (Setup), which puts the task back into setup.

requestBody.description:
A JSON array of row decisions (not an object). Send an empty array with status 3 to complete the task with the decisions already saved.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): ID of the activity row. Rows that are not in the task are ignored.
- `status` (integer, required): Decision for the row: 2 (Approved) or 3 (Denied). Rows with status NotSet (0) are left unchanged. Send only 2 or 3.

200.description: Returns the task summary and the detail of each activity row.

400.description: The task is in setup or already complete, or the review failed.

401.description: The signed-in user is not the reviewer for this task.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The task does not exist.

get.summary: List task activity rows for review
get.description:
Returns a page of the activity rows in a task that is released for review, so the assigned reviewer can approve or deny them. Each row shows the user, access policy, resource, credential, activity and last access time.

Permission required: Reviewer role.

Values for `data[].status`: 0 = NotSet, 1 = Requested, 2 = Approved, 3 = Denied.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The ID of the access certification task.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Text to search for, ignoring case. Returns only rows whose user, access policy, resource, credential, activity or connection profile contains this text.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. Applies only when orderBy is set.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of items to skip before returning results. The default is 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Number of items to return. The default is 10.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Name of the property to sort the results by, ignoring case. When omitted, results sort by user name in ascending order.

200.description: Returns a table object with the page of items in data and the total number of matching items in recordsTotal.

400.description: The request failed, or the task is still being set up.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The task does not exist.

put.summary: Select the activity rows for a task
put.description:
Adds or removes activity rows in a task. A row with no ID and status Requested (1) is added, and a row with an ID and status NotSet (0) is removed. Build the rows from the activitiesDetail list that the create, update or get task call returns.

Permission required: Admin role.

Values for `rows[].status and activitiesDetail[].status`: 0 = NotSet, 1 = Requested, 2 = Approved, 3 = Denied.

Values for `summary.status`: 0 = Setup, 1 = ReadyToStart, 2 = Incomplete, 3 = Complete.

Caution: Changes are saved immediately. The server does not check the task's status, so rows can still be added or removed after the task is released for review.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The ID of the access certification task.

requestBody.description:
The task ID and the rows to add or remove.

- `taskId` (string (GUID), required): ID of the task. It must match the ID in the path.
- `rows` (array of row objects, required): The rows to change, in the same shape as activitiesDetail in the task response. Set status on each row to add or remove it. Each row's userId is the task's own user entry, as returned in activitiesDetail, not the user account ID. To add a row, leave id empty (or omit it), set status to 1 (Requested), and copy accessPolicyId, activityId, resourceId, credentialId and userId from an available row. To remove a row, send its id with status 0 (NotSet). Rows that do not match a row available to the task are ignored.

200.description: Returns the task summary and the detail of each activity row, selected and available.

400.description: The ID in the path does not match the body, or the update failed.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The task does not exist.

get.summary: List task activity rows
get.description:
Returns a page of the activity rows selected for a task. Each row shows the user, access policy, resource, credential, activity and last access time.

Permission required: Admin role.

Values for `data[].status`: 0 = NotSet, 1 = Requested, 2 = Approved, 3 = Denied.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The ID of the access certification task.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Text to search for, ignoring case. Returns only rows whose user, access policy, resource, credential, activity or connection profile contains this text.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. Applies only when orderBy is set.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of items to skip before returning results. The default is 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Number of items to return. The default is 10.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Name of the property to sort the results by, ignoring case. When omitted, results sort by user name in ascending order.

200.description: Returns a table object with the page of items in data and the total number of matching items in recordsTotal.

400.description: The request failed.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The task does not exist.

get.summary: List access certification tasks
get.description:
Returns every access certification task with its name, status, reviewer and dates, sorted by name.

Permission required: Admin role.

Values for `[].status`: 0 = Setup, 1 = ReadyToStart, 2 = Incomplete, 3 = Complete.

200.description: Returns an array of task summaries. The array is empty when there are no tasks.

400.description: The tasks could not be retrieved.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

delete.description:
Deletes an access certification task. A task that is already complete cannot be deleted.

Permission required: Admin role.

Caution: The task is deleted immediately and the call cannot be undone.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The ID of the task to delete.

202.description: The delete was accepted.

400.description: The task is complete or could not be deleted.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The task does not exist.

post.description:
Creates a task in the Setup (0) state and returns it with the activity rows available for its users. Use the rows update call afterward to choose which rows to include.

Permission required: Admin role.

Values for `summary.status`: 0 = Setup, 1 = ReadyToStart, 2 = Incomplete, 3 = Complete.

Values for `activitiesDetail[].status`: 0 = NotSet, 1 = Requested, 2 = Approved, 3 = Denied.

Caution: The task is created immediately.

requestBody.description:
The task to create.

- `name` (string, required): Name of the task. Must be unique across tasks, ignoring case.
- `description` (string): Description of the task.
- `reviewerId` (string (GUID), required): ID of the user who reviews the task. Only this user can see and review the task. The server does not check this value, so always set it.
- `userIds` (array of string (GUID)): IDs of the users whose access the task covers.
- `groupIds` (array of string (GUID)): IDs of the user groups whose members' access the task covers. The members of each group are added as users of the task when it is saved.
- `scheduledStartDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Scheduled start time in UTC. Ignored on create. The server sets the scheduled start to the creation time.
- `startDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Start time in UTC. Leave it out. A value sent on create is stored as given; otherwise the server sets it when the reviewer first saves a review with status Incomplete (2).
- `id` (string (GUID)): ID of the task. Leave it out when creating a task.
- `status` (integer): Task status. Ignored on create. The server sets the status to Setup (0).

200.description: Returns the task summary and the detail of each available activity row.

400.description: The name is missing or the task could not be created.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

409.description: A task with this name already exists. Names are compared ignoring case.

put.summary: Update or release an access certification task
put.description:
Replaces the settings of a task that is still in the Setup (0) state, including its name, description, reviewer, users and status. Set status to ReadyToStart (1) to release the task for review; after that, this call no longer accepts changes. Changing the users can change which activity rows are available, so check the row selection afterward with the rows update call, using the rows this call returns.

Permission required: Admin role.

Values for `summary.status`: 0 = Setup, 1 = ReadyToStart, 2 = Incomplete, 3 = Complete.

Values for `activitiesDetail[].status`: 0 = NotSet, 1 = Requested, 2 = Approved, 3 = Denied.

Caution: The call replaces the whole task immediately, so any field or user you leave out is cleared. Send the same task ID in the path and the body: only the task in the path is checked for the Setup state, but the task in the body is the one changed.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The ID of the task to update.

requestBody.description:
The complete task. Values you leave out are cleared, so send every field you want to keep.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): ID of the task. Send the same ID as in the path. The server does not check that this matches the ID in the path. The task with this ID is the one updated, so always send the path ID.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the task. The server does not check that the new name is unique.
- `description` (string): Description of the task.
- `reviewerId` (string (GUID), required): ID of the user who reviews the task. The server does not check this value, so always set it.
- `status` (integer): Task status. Send 0 (Setup) to keep editing, or 1 (ReadyToStart) to release the task for review. If you leave it out, it is set to Setup (0).
- `userIds` (array of string (GUID)): IDs of the users whose access the task covers. Replaces the task's current users. An empty or missing list removes all users.
- `groupIds` (array of string (GUID)): IDs of the user groups whose members' access the task covers. The members of each group are added as users of the task when it is saved.
- `scheduledStartDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Scheduled start time in UTC. Send the current value to keep it.
- `startDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Start time in UTC. Ignored. The server keeps the stored value.

200.description: Returns the task summary and the detail of each available activity row.

400.description: The task has already been released for review, or the update failed.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The task does not exist.

get.summary: List access certification tasks for a reviewer
get.description:
Returns the tasks assigned to one reviewer, sorted by name. Tasks that are still in setup are never returned.

Permission required: Reviewer role.

Values for `[].status`: 0 = Setup, 1 = ReadyToStart, 2 = Incomplete, 3 = Complete.

Caution: The response lists the tasks assigned to the reviewer ID you supply.

parameters.name: reviewerId
parameters.description: The ID of the reviewer.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only tasks with this status number. Omit it to return all tasks that are not in setup.

200.description: Returns an array of task summaries.

400.description: The tasks could not be retrieved.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

get.summary: List task users for review
get.description:
Returns a page of the users covered by a task that is released for review, with their email address and account name.

Permission required: Reviewer role.

Values for `data[].type`: 0 = User, 1 = Application, 2 = Local.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The ID of the access certification task.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Text to search for, ignoring case. Returns only users whose name, email address or account name contains this text.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. Applies only when orderBy is set.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of items to skip before returning results. The default is 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Number of items to return. The default is 10.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Name of the property to sort the results by, ignoring case. When omitted, results sort by user name in ascending order.

200.description: Returns a table object with the page of items in data and the total number of matching items in recordsTotal.

400.description: The request failed, or the task is still being set up.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The task does not exist.

get.summary: List task users
get.description:
Returns a page of the users covered by a task, with their email address and account name.

Permission required: Admin role.

Values for `data[].type`: 0 = User, 1 = Application, 2 = Local.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The ID of the access certification task.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Text to search for, ignoring case. Returns only users whose name, email address or account name contains this text.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. Applies only when orderBy is set.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of items to skip before returning results. The default is 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Number of items to return. The default is 10.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Name of the property to sort the results by, ignoring case. When omitted, results sort by user name in ascending order.

200.description: Returns a table object with the page of items in data and the total number of matching items in recordsTotal.

400.description: The request failed.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The task does not exist.

get.summary: Get an access certification task
get.description:
Returns one task with its summary and the detail of each activity row.

Permission required: Admin or Reviewer role.

Values for `summary.status`: 0 = Setup, 1 = ReadyToStart, 2 = Incomplete, 3 = Complete.

Values for `activitiesDetail[].status`: 0 = NotSet, 1 = Requested, 2 = Approved, 3 = Denied.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: The ID of the task to retrieve.

200.description: Returns the task summary and the detail of each activity row.

400.description: The task could not be retrieved.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The task does not exist.

get.summary: List access policies
get.description:
Returns the access policies. With no options it returns every access policy, including deleted and disabled ones. Use isDeleted or isDisabled to return only those.

Permission required: Administrator role or application role.

parameters.name: isDeleted
parameters.description: Set to true to return only deleted access policies. False has no effect.

parameters.name: isDisabled
parameters.description: Set to true to return only disabled access policies. If isDeleted is also true, isDeleted wins. False has no effect.

parameters.name: ignoreStatus
parameters.description: Returns all access policies, the same as leaving all three options off.

200.description: Returns an array of access policies.

400.description: The access policies could not be retrieved.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role or permission.

post.description:
Creates an access policy and returns it with its new id. A policy is either Resource based, which lets users run the policy activities on its resources, or Credential based, which lets users release a credential during a session. A Credential based policy automatically gets the Credential Release and File Release activities. The name must be unique among all access policies. Add members afterwards with the add routes.

Permission required: Administrator or application.

Values for `policyType`: 0 = Resource, 1 = Credential.

requestBody.description:
The access policy to create. The notesRequired, ticketRequired and approvalTypeRequired fields that appear in responses are ignored when sent.

- `name` (string, required): Unique name of the policy. A duplicate name is rejected. The check ignores upper and lower case.
- `description` (string): Description of the policy.
- `policyType` (integer (enum)): Whether the policy is Resource based or Credential based. 0 = Resource, 1 = Credential. If omitted, the policy is Resource based.
- `activityConfigurationId` (string (GUID), required): Id of the connection profile that the policy uses, as returned by the connection profile list. Required.
- `priority` (integer): Priority of the policy.

200.description: The policy was created. The body is the new policy with its id. In it, approvalTypeRequired is always 0, notesRequired and ticketRequired are false and activityConfiguration is null; read the policy back with the Get route for current values.

400.description: The name is missing or already used by another policy, the connection profile id is missing, or the policy could not be created.

get.summary: List activity cards with their access policies
get.description:
Returns the activities available to a managed account as cards, together with the access policy details for each. Administrators can request another account; other users always see their own.

Permission required: Any signed-in user.

parameters.name: managedAccountId
parameters.description: ID of the managed account. Only administrators can use it to view another account; for other users it is ignored.

parameters.name: Skip
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before returning results. Default is 0.

parameters.name: Take
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return. Default is 100.

parameters.name: OrderBy
parameters.description: Name of the property to sort the results by.

parameters.name: OrderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. Default is false.

parameters.name: FilterText
parameters.description: Returns only cards whose activity name or access policy name contains this text.

parameters.name: FilterColumns
parameters.description: Not used by this route. The server accepts it but ignores it.

parameters.name: groupByPolicy
parameters.description: Set to true to group the cards by access policy.

parameters.name: includeCount
parameters.description: Not used in this release. The server accepts it but ignores it.

parameters.name: includeData
parameters.description: Not used in this release. The server accepts it but ignores it; the card data is always returned.

200.description: Returns a table object with the total record count and the requested page of activity cards.

400.description: No managed account could be determined, for example when an administrator signs in without a managed account and passes no managedAccountId.

get.summary: List resources a user can start an activity session on
get.description:
Returns the resources that the signed-in user can use to start an activity session, optionally narrowed to one activity and one access policy. Administrators can pass a managed account to see the list for that account.

Permission required: Any signed-in user.

parameters.name: activityId
parameters.description: Limit results to resources usable for this activity.

parameters.name: policyId
parameters.description: Limit results to this access policy.

parameters.name: managedAccountId
parameters.description: ID of the managed account to list resources for. Only administrators can use it; for other users it is ignored.

parameters.name: Skip
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before returning results. Default is 0.

parameters.name: Take
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return. Default is 100.

parameters.name: OrderBy
parameters.description: Name of the property to sort the results by.

parameters.name: OrderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. Default is false.

parameters.name: FilterText
parameters.description: Returns only records that contain this text. The properties searched depend on the route.

parameters.name: FilterColumns
parameters.description: Not used by this route. The server accepts it but ignores it.

200.description: Returns a table object with the total record count and the requested page of resources.

400.description: No managed account could be determined for the request.

post.summary: Add managed account group to multiple access policies
post.description:
Adds the managed account group to every access policy in the list that exists, in one call. Ids that match no policy are ignored. Use it to give the managed account group access through several policies at once.

Permission required: Administrator.

Caution: The change applies immediately and affects who can access resources through each listed policy.

parameters.name: managedAccountGroupId
parameters.description: The id of the managed account group.

requestBody.description:
The ids of the access policies to add the managed account group to.

- `(array item)` (string (GUID), required): Id of an access policy. The body is a JSON array of ids and must not be empty.

200.description: The call finished. The body is a short text message that says the group was added to one policy or N policies, where N is the number of listed policies that exist, including ones where nothing needed to change. An unknown group id also returns this message, and nothing is added.

400.description: No group or no policies were supplied, none of the listed ids is an existing policy, or the change failed.

post.summary: Add managed account to multiple access policies
post.description:
Adds the managed account to every access policy in the list that exists, in one call. Ids that match no policy are ignored. Use it to give the managed account access through several policies at once.

Permission required: Administrator.

Caution: The change applies immediately and affects who can access resources through each listed policy.

parameters.name: managedAccountId
parameters.description: The id of the managed account.

requestBody.description:
The ids of the access policies to add the managed account to.

- `(array item)` (string (GUID), required): Id of an access policy. The body is a JSON array of ids and must not be empty.

200.description: The change was made. The body is a short text message that says the account was added to one policy or N policies, where N is the number of listed policies that exist, including ones where nothing needed to change.

400.description: No account or no policies were supplied, none of the listed ids is an existing policy, the managed account does not exist, or the change failed.

put.description:
Creates a new access policy from an existing one and returns it. The new policy takes its settings from the body you send, and keeps the accounts, account groups, user and group collections and credentials of the source policy; a resource-based copy also keeps the resources, resource groups and activities.

Permission required: Administrator.

Values for `policyType`: 0 = Resource, 1 = Credential.

requestBody.description:
The source policy id and the settings of the new policy. The new policy takes its name, description, priority, connection profile and policy type from the body, not from the source.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): Id of the policy to copy.
- `name` (string, required): Name for the new policy. The server does not check that the name is unique, so use a name that is not already taken.
- `activityConfigurationId` (string (GUID), required): Id of the connection profile for the new policy. A copy without it fails.
- `description` (string): Description of the new policy.
- `priority` (integer): Priority of the new policy. If omitted, the priority is 0.
- `policyType` (integer (enum)): Whether the new policy is Resource based or Credential based. 0 = Resource, 1 = Credential. If omitted, the copy is Resource based even when the source is Credential based, so send the type of the source policy.

200.description: The copy was created. The body is the new policy.

400.description: No policy id was sent, a required value such as the name or connection profile is missing, or the copy failed.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator.

get.summary: Look up the activities in an access policy
get.description:
Returns a map of activity ID to activity name for the activities in the access policy, including activities that come from activity groups. A deleted activity appears with the name "Deleted Activity".

Permission required: Administrator role, or a user whose custom role grants the Access Policies permission for this access policy.

parameters.name: policyId
parameters.description: ID of the access policy.

200.description: Returns an object whose keys are activity IDs and whose values are activity names.

400.description: The lookup failed. The body contains an error message.

401.description: The signed-in user is not allowed to work with this access policy.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role or permission.

404.description: The access policy does not exist.

get.summary: Look up the credentials in an access policy
get.description:
Returns a map of credential ID to credential name for a credential access policy, including credentials that come from credential groups. Calling it on a policy of another type returns an error.

Permission required: Administrator role, or a user whose custom role grants the Access Policies permission for this access policy.

parameters.name: policyId
parameters.description: ID of the credential access policy.

200.description: Returns an object whose keys are credential IDs and whose values are credential names.

400.description: The lookup failed, for example because the policy is not a credential policy.

401.description: The signed-in user is not allowed to work with this access policy.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role or permission.

404.description: The access policy does not exist.

get.summary: Look up the resources in an access policy
get.description:
Returns a map of resource ID to resource name for a resource access policy, including resources that come from resource groups. Calling it on a policy of another type returns an error.

Permission required: Administrator role, or a user whose custom role grants the Access Policies permission for this access policy.

parameters.name: policyId
parameters.description: ID of the resource access policy.

200.description: Returns an object whose keys are resource IDs and whose values are resource names.

400.description: The lookup failed, for example because the policy is not a resource policy.

401.description: The signed-in user is not allowed to work with this access policy.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role or permission.

404.description: The access policy does not exist.

delete.summary: Remove a managed account from all access policies
delete.description:
Removes the managed account's direct assignment from every enabled access policy that applies to it. Access the account gets through a managed account group or collection is not changed. The response lists the access policies that were found for the account.

Permission required: Administrator role.

parameters.name: managedAccountId
parameters.description: ID of the managed account to remove from access policies.

202.description: The removal finished. The body lists the access policies that were found for the account.

400.description: The managed account was not found or the removal failed.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role or permission.

get.summary: List activity cards for a managed account
get.description:
Returns the activity cards and access policy details for a managed account. Administrators can view any account; other users can view only their own.

Permission required: Any signed-in user (own account), or Administrator role for any account.

parameters.name: managedAccountId
parameters.description: ID of the managed account.

parameters.name: Skip
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before returning results. Default is 0.

parameters.name: Take
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return. Default is 100.

put.description:
Updates the settings of an access policy and returns the updated policy. The id in the body must match the id in the path, and the name must stay unique. The settings you send replace the stored values. The member lists in the body only add members; change membership with the add and remove routes.

Permission required: Administrator, application, or a custom role with the Modify Name, Modify Description or Modify Connection Profile permission on this policy.

Values for `policyType`: 0 = Resource, 1 = Credential.

Caution: Settings left out of the body are reset: the description is cleared, the priority becomes 0 and the policy type becomes Resource. The update also clears the disabled and deleted flags, and removes members that do not fit the policy type: a Resource policy loses its credentials, secret vaults and Credential Release and File Release activities; a Credential policy loses its resource groups, its resources other than secret vaults, its activity groups and its activities other than Credential Release and File Release. Members listed in the body are added before the name is checked, so a request rejected for a duplicate name can still add them. Send every setting you want to keep.

parameters.name: accessControlPolicyId
parameters.description: The id of the access policy to update.

requestBody.description:
The access policy settings. Start from the policy returned by the Get route and change only what you need; the settings you send replace the stored ones.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): Id of the policy. It must match the id in the path.
- `name` (string, required): Unique name of the policy. A duplicate name is rejected. The check ignores upper and lower case.
- `description` (string): Description of the policy. If omitted, the description is cleared.
- `policyType` (integer (enum)): Whether the policy is Resource based or Credential based. 0 = Resource, 1 = Credential. If omitted, the policy becomes Resource based.
- `priority` (integer): Priority of the policy. If omitted, the priority is set to 0.
- `activityConfigurationId` (string (GUID), required): Id of the connection profile that the policy uses. If omitted, the update fails.
- `managedAccountIds` (array of string (GUID)): Ids of accounts to add to the policy. Ids already in the policy are kept. Accounts left out of the list are not removed by this route; use the Remove routes for that.
- `managedAccountGroupIds` (array of string (GUID)): Ids of account groups to add to the policy. Ids already in the policy are kept. Account groups left out of the list are not removed by this route; use the Remove routes for that.
- `managedResourceIds` (array of string (GUID)): Ids of resources to add to the policy. Ids already in the policy are kept. Resources left out of the list are not removed by this route; use the Remove routes for that.
- `managedResourceGroupIds` (array of string (GUID)): Ids of resource groups to add to the policy. Ids already in the policy are kept. Resource groups left out of the list are not removed by this route; use the Remove routes for that.

200.description: The updated policy. In it, approvalTypeRequired is always 0, notesRequired and ticketRequired are false and activityConfiguration is null; read the connection profile with its own route.

400.description: The id in the body does not match the path, the name is missing or not unique, the connection profile is missing, a listed member does not exist or does not fit the policy type, or the update failed.

401.description: A custom-role user is not allowed to change this policy.

403.description: The caller is not allowed to update policies.

get.summary: List all action groups
get.description:
Returns every action group, each with its actions. An action group is an ordered set of actions that an activity runs before, during or after a session.

Permission required: Administrator role or the application role.

200.description: An array of action groups.

401.description: The request is not signed in.

403.description: The signed-in account does not have the required role.

post.description:
Creates an action group. The server sets the creation and modification details from the signed-in account.

Permission required: Administrator role or the application role.

requestBody.description:
The action group to create.

- `name` (string): The name of the action group.
- `description` (string): A description of the action group.
- `action` (array): The actions in the group, each in the action format. Leave this empty and add actions after the group exists with the create action route.

201.description: The action group was created. The body is the new group and the Location value points to it.

401.description: The request is not signed in.

403.description: The signed-in account does not have the required role.

post.summary: Create an action in an action group
post.description:
Adds a new action to the end of an existing action group and updates the group modified details. If you send no parameters, the action gets the template's default parameter values. When the template needs a paired action and you include pairedAction, the paired action is created as well.

Permission required: Administrator role or the application role.

Values for `classification`: 0 = PreSession, 1 = Session, 2 = PostSession, 3 = Internal, 4 = Any.

Caution: This call takes effect immediately and changes the steps that run in later sessions for the activity that uses the action group.

requestBody.description:
The action to create.

- `actionGroupId` (string (GUID), required): The action group the action belongs to. The group must already exist.
- `actionTemplateId` (string (GUID), required): The action template the action is built from. Get template IDs from the action template list.
- `actionParameter` (array): One entry per template parameter, each with actionTemplateParameterId and value. If you send no entries, the server creates one per template parameter with its default value. If you send entries, they replace the defaults.
- `displayName` (string): The name shown for the action.
- `classification` (integer): When the action runs relative to the session. Send the classification of the action template. The server sets the classification from the action template and the response shows the template value. See classification values.
- `continueOnFail` (boolean): When true, the next action in the group still runs if this one fails.
- `executionOrder` (integer): Ignored on create. The new action is always added at the end of the group. Change the position afterwards with the update action route.
- `timeout` (integer): Seconds after which the action is failed if it has not completed. The default is 300 when you leave the field out.
- `pairedActionId` (string (GUID)): The identifier of an existing action to record as the pair of this one. It is set to null if no action has that identifier. Usually left out; send pairedAction instead.
- `pairedAction` (object): For templates that come in pairs, an object with a displayName for the paired action that the server creates. Used only when the action template requires a pair. The action group must belong to an activity, or the request fails.
- `executionPath` (string): Runs the action only when an earlier action in the group returned this execution path. Leave it empty to run the action on every path.

201.description: The action was created. The body is the new action and the Location value points to it.

401.description: The request is not signed in.

403.description: The signed-in account does not have the required role.

500.description: The request failed, for example because the action group does not exist, or a paired action is needed and the action group does not belong to an activity.

200.description: The log entry, with its type, time, message and version.

400.description: The request failed; the body holds the error text.

get.summary: Search action queues with paging
get.description:
Returns a page of action queue runs with their job, activity, resource and account details. Use it to find and review runs; the console uses it for its action queue list.

Permission required: Requires the Admin, Auditing and Reporting, or App role.

Values for `status`: -4 = Paused, -3 = Scheduled, -2 = Unknown, -1 = Pending, 0 = Queued, 1 = Running, 2 = Complete, 3 = Failed, 4 = Cancelled, 5 = CompletedWithErrors, 6 = CompletedNotRun.

Values for `jobType`: 0 = None, 1 = Protection, 2 = PasswordRotation, 3 = PasswordVerification, 4 = HostScan, 5 = DomainSync, 6 = DomainSyncTest, 7 = ActivitySession, 8 = RemoteServiceRegistration, 9 = ServiceRotation, 10 = PasswordRollback, 11 = DomainOUMapping, 12 = ResourceConnectionTest, 13 = WinRmHttp, 14 = Report, 15 = Debug, 16 = CommandPlanRun.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Returns only runs whose job name contains this text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Name of the field to sort by. Default is startTimeUtc.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: When true (default), sorts in descending order.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of items to skip. Default is 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Maximum number of items to return. Default is 100.

200.description: An object with data, the page of matching runs, and recordsTotal, the total count. Without filterText, recordsTotal counts every action queue.

400.description: The search failed; the body holds the error text.

delete.description:
Sets the status of the action queue to Cancelled (4). Use it to cancel an action queue that is queued or running.

Permission required: Requires the Admin, Auditing and Reporting, or App role.

Caution: The status changes to Cancelled immediately, and the call does not check whether the action queue has already finished.

parameters.name: actionQueueId
parameters.description: ID of the action queue to cancel.

202.description: The action queue status is set to Cancelled.

400.description: The cancel failed; the body holds the error text.

404.description: No action queue has this ID.

get.summary: Get an action queue
get.description:
Returns one action queue, including its status and status description. Use it to check progress of a run you started.

Permission required: Requires the Admin, Auditing and Reporting, or App role.

Values for `status`: -4 = Paused, -3 = Scheduled, -2 = Unknown, -1 = Pending, 0 = Queued, 1 = Running, 2 = Complete, 3 = Failed, 4 = Cancelled, 5 = CompletedWithErrors, 6 = CompletedNotRun.

Values for `failureReason`: 0 = NoError, 1 = UnknownError, 2 = SystemError, 3 = ActionServiceUnavailable, 4 = ActionTimeout, 5 = AccessDenied, 6 = UserAlreadyMemberofGroup, 7 = UserNotMemberofGroup, 8 = InvalidGroupName, 9 = InvalidUserName, 10 = InvalidHostName, 11 = FailedToConnect.

parameters.name: actionQueueId
parameters.description: ID of the action queue.

200.description: The action queue.

400.description: The request failed; the body holds the error text.

404.description: No action queue has this ID.

get.summary: Get the job behind an action queue
get.description:
Returns the scheduled job that created the action queue, including its schedule and type. Use it to see when and how a run was scheduled.

Permission required: Requires the Admin, Auditing and Reporting, or App role.

Values for `type`: 0 = None, 1 = Protection, 2 = PasswordRotation, 3 = PasswordVerification, 4 = HostScan, 5 = DomainSync, 6 = DomainSyncTest, 7 = ActivitySession, 8 = RemoteServiceRegistration, 9 = ServiceRotation, 10 = PasswordRollback, 11 = DomainOUMapping, 12 = ResourceConnectionTest, 13 = WinRmHttp, 14 = Report, 15 = Debug, 16 = CommandPlanRun.

Values for `recurrenceType`: 0 = None, 1 = Minutes, 2 = Daily, 3 = Weekly, 4 = Monthly.

parameters.name: actionQueueId
parameters.description: ID of the action queue.

200.description: The job.

404.description: No job exists for this action queue.

get.summary: Get log entries for an action queue
get.description:
Returns a page of log entries for an action queue. Use it to follow or review a run, filtering by level or text.

Permission required: Requires the Admin, Auditing and Reporting, or App role.

Values for `logLevel`: 0 = Debug, 1 = Info, 2 = Warn, 3 = Error.

parameters.name: actionQueueId
parameters.description: ID of the action queue whose log to read.

parameters.name: lastRunActionQueueId
parameters.description: ID of another action queue run. When set, entries from that run are returned together with entries from the action queue in the path.

parameters.name: logLevel
parameters.description: Minimum log level, sent as a number: returns entries at this level or higher. 0 Debug, 1 Info, 2 Warn, 3 Error. When omitted, 0 is used and all entries are returned.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of log entries to skip. Default is 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Maximum number of log entries to return. Default is 10.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: When true (default), returns the newest entries first.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Returns only entries whose message contains this text, ignoring case.

200.description: An object with the log lines, the total count of matching entries, and a version.

400.description: The ID is empty or the search failed.

get.summary: List action templates you can choose from
get.description:
Returns the action templates available for selection when building activities, with their parameters. Templates that are not available for selection are left out. Returns an empty array when there are none.

Permission required: Requires the Admin or App role.

Values for `classification`: 0 = PreSession, 1 = Session, 2 = PostSession, 3 = Internal, 4 = Any.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Accepted for compatibility but not applied; all templates are returned. A negative value returns 400.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Accepted for compatibility but not applied; all templates are returned. A negative value returns 400.

200.description: An array of action templates, each with its parameters.

400.description: Skip or take is negative.

post.summary: Create a template from an action step
post.description:
Creates a new user-defined action template from an existing action step and returns it. The template is named after the step (or after the step's own template when the step has no name) and copies the description, definition, icon and parameters from the step's template. A parameter that has a value on the step becomes optional, with that value as its default. The classification is not copied, so the new template has classification 0 (PreSession).

Permission required: Requires the Admin or App role.

Values for `classification`: 0 = PreSession, 1 = Session, 2 = PostSession, 3 = Internal, 4 = Any.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: ID of the action step to turn into a template.

200.description: The new action template.

400.description: No action step has this ID, or a user-defined template with the same name already exists; the body holds the error text.

get.summary: Get one action template parameter by its ID
get.description:
Returns a single action template parameter, such as its name, type, whether it is required and its default value. The ID in the path is matched against the parameter's own ID, not the template's; to list all parameters of a template, get the template and read its actionTemplateParameter array.

Permission required: Requires the Admin or App role.

Values for `type`: 0 = PowerShell, 1 = Integer, 2 = DateTime, 3 = Credential, 4 = SecureString, 5 = String, 6 = KeyValue, 7 = Guid, 8 = HostId, 9 = UserId, 10 = ManagedResourceId, 11 = ManagedAccountId, 12 = UserCredential, 13 = DomainId, 14 = SessionId, 15 = DomainCredential, 16 = DomainConfigurationId, 17 = Boolean, 18 = ReportId.

parameters.name: templateId
parameters.description: ID of the template parameter (not the template).

200.description: The template parameter.

404.description: No template parameter has this ID.

get.summary: List user-defined action templates
get.description:
Returns the action templates that users created, with optional paging. Returns an empty array when there are none.

Permission required: Requires the Admin or App role.

Values for `classification`: 0 = PreSession, 1 = Session, 2 = PostSession, 3 = Internal, 4 = Any.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of templates to skip. Must not be negative.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Maximum number of templates to return. Must not be negative.

200.description: An array of action templates.

400.description: Skip or take is negative.

delete.description:
Deletes the action template with the given ID and its parameters. If the template is one half of a start/end pair, the paired template is deleted too.

Permission required: Requires the Admin or App role.

Caution: The template, and its paired template if it has one, is deleted immediately and cannot be restored through the API.

parameters.name: templateId
parameters.description: ID of the template to delete.

202.description: The template is deleted. The body is empty.

404.description: No template has this ID.

get.summary: Get an action template
get.description:
Returns one action template, including its parameters. Use it to see which values an action built from the template needs.

Permission required: Requires the Admin or App role.

Values for `classification`: 0 = PreSession, 1 = Session, 2 = PostSession, 3 = Internal, 4 = Any.

parameters.name: templateId
parameters.description: ID of the template.

200.description: A single action template object.

404.description: No template has this ID.

put.description:
Updates the action template's own settings, such as its name, description, definition and icon, with the values you send. The template is found by the id in the body, and the display name must be unique among templates. Parameters are not changed by this call.

Permission required: Requires the Admin or App role.

Values for `classification`: 0 = PreSession, 1 = Session, 2 = PostSession, 3 = Internal, 4 = Any.

Caution: The change applies immediately. Settings left out of the body are reset to defaults, including classification (to 0, PreSession) and userDefined (to false).

parameters.name: templateId
parameters.description: ID of the template to update.

requestBody.description:
The action template. Send every setting you want to keep, because any setting you omit, including those not listed here, is reset to its default.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): ID of the template being updated. The template is looked up by this value; use the same ID as in the path.
- `displayName` (string, required): Name of the template. Must not match another template's name, ignoring case; otherwise 400.
- `description` (string): Description of the template.
- `definition` (string): Definition of the template.
- `icon` (string): Icon for the template.
- `classification` (integer (enum)): When the step can run, sent as a number. See the values below.
- `actionTemplateParameter` (array): Parameters of the template. Ignored by this call; parameters are not updated.
- `userDefined` (boolean): Whether users created the template. Omitting it sets false, which removes the template from the user-defined list.
- `newActionDisplayName` (string): Default name for a new action built from the template.
- `pairedActionTemplateId` (string (GUID)): ID of the paired start or end template. Omitting it clears the pairing link on this template.
- `actionPackId` (string (GUID)): ID of the action pack that contains the template.

200.description: The updated template.

400.description: Another template already uses that name.

500.description: No template has the ID in the body, or displayName is missing.

get.summary: Get a domain by name
get.description:
Looks up a domain by its fully qualified or NetBIOS name and returns its configuration ID and both names.

Permission required: Requires the Admin or App role.

parameters.name: domainName
parameters.description: Fully qualified or NetBIOS name of the domain.

200.description: An object with domainConfigId, fqdn and netbios.

400.description: The lookup failed; the body holds the error text.

404.description: No domain has this name.

get.summary: Get Active Directory properties of a user
get.description:
Returns the directory attributes of a user as key and value pairs. Use it to inspect an account in a domain.

Permission required: Requires the Admin or App role.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Name of the domain. Also used as the server to query unless domainController is set.

parameters.name: samaccountname
parameters.description: The user's sAMAccountName.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: ID of a stored user. When set, that user's domain name replaces the domain in the path for the lookup. The server queried is still the path domain, or domainController when set.

parameters.name: domainController
parameters.description: Domain controller to query instead of the domain.

200.description: An array of objects with key and value.

400.description: The lookup failed; the body holds the error text.

404.description: The user was not found.

get.summary: List domain IDs with their domain controller names
get.description:
Returns the ID of each Active Directory domain that has a domain controller, with the domain controller name as the name, sorted by that name.

Permission required: Requires the Admin or App role.

200.description: An array of objects with id and name, where name is the domain controller name.

get.summary: List all activities
get.description:
Returns every activity that has not been deleted, with its settings and the activity groups it belongs to. Credential release and file release activities are not included.

Permission required: Administrator role. The signed-in session must have completed multifactor authentication.

200.description: An array of activities.

post.description:
Creates an activity. If you do not supply the start, during and end step groups, the server creates an empty group for each and returns their ids. The creation is recorded in the event log.

Permission required: Administrator role. The signed-in session must have completed multifactor authentication.

Values for `activityType`: 0 = Interactive, 1 = InteractiveAppLaunch, 2 = TaskAutomation, 3 = CredentialRelease, 4 = FileRelease.

Values for `loginAccount`: 0 = Requester, 1 = Managed, 2 = ActivityIdentity (shown as Activity Token in the console), 3 = Vault, 4 = Resource.

Values for `requesterLoginFormat`: 0 = Samaccountname (Domain\SamAccountName), 1 = UPN (User Principal Name), 2 = Email, 3 = SamAccountNameOnly (SamAccountName), 4 = Custom.

Caution: The activity is created immediately and can start applying wherever it is later added to an access policy.

requestBody.description:
The activity to create.

- `id` (string (GUID)): Identifier of the activity. On update it must match the id in the path. On copy it identifies the activity to copy.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the activity. Must be unique among activities, up to 256 characters.
- `description` (string): Description of the activity.
- `platformId` (string (GUID)): Platform the activity applies to. Use the Platform names list to find the id.
- `activityType` (integer): Kind of activity. See the `Values for activityType` paragraph in the operation description.
- `loginAccount` (integer): Type of account the activity signs in with. See the `Values for loginAccount` paragraph in the operation description.
- `loginAccountNameFormat` (string): Template for the sign-in account name, for example one built from %samaccountname%. Required and validated unless loginAccount is Requester or Vault. An invalid template returns 400 with a message.
- `requesterLoginFormat` (integer): Name format to use when the requester is the sign-in account. See the `Values for requesterLoginFormat` paragraph in the operation description.
- `applicationToLaunch` (string): Path of the application to launch for application-launch activities.
- `preferredRDSHostId` (string (GUID)): Resource to use as the preferred Remote Desktop Services host.
- `connectCredentialId` (string (GUID)): Service account used to connect to the Remote Desktop Services host.
- `createAccount` (boolean): Whether to create the account when the session starts. Applies when loginAccount is Managed or Resource.
- `deleteAccount` (boolean): Whether to delete the account when the session ends. When false the account is disabled. Applies when loginAccount is Managed or Resource.
- `vaultId` (string (GUID)): Vault connector used to look up the sign-in credentials. Used when loginAccount is Vault.
- `vaultInfo` (string): Vault-specific settings, as a JSON string. Used when loginAccount is Vault.
- `logonUrl` (string): Sign-in URL for website activities.
- `activityConfigurationId` (string (GUID)): Connection profile settings attached to the activity.
- `startActionGroupId` (string (GUID)): Steps that run when a session starts. If omitted, null or the empty GUID on create, an empty step group is created and its id is returned. On update, omitted ids keep their current values.
- `duringActionGroupId` (string (GUID)): Steps that run during a session. Same behavior as startActionGroupId.
- `endActionGroupId` (string (GUID)): Steps that run when a session ends. Same behavior as startActionGroupId.

201.description: The activity is created. The response body is the new activity, and the Location header points to it.

400.description: The sign-in account name template is missing or invalid. The response body is the error message as plain text.

500.description: The activity could not be created, for example because another activity already has the same name.

post.description:
Creates a new activity from an existing one. Set the id in the request body to the activity to copy and supply the settings for the new activity, including a new name. Settings you leave out take default values; they are not copied from the original activity. The copy gets its own copies of the original's start, during and end steps, and, when the body includes a connection profile id, its own copy of the original activity's connection profile settings. The creation is recorded in the event log.

Permission required: Administrator role. The signed-in session must have completed multifactor authentication.

Values for `activityType`: 0 = Interactive, 1 = InteractiveAppLaunch, 2 = TaskAutomation, 3 = CredentialRelease, 4 = FileRelease.

Values for `loginAccount`: 0 = Requester, 1 = Managed, 2 = ActivityIdentity (shown as Activity Token in the console), 3 = Vault, 4 = Resource.

Values for `requesterLoginFormat`: 0 = Samaccountname (Domain\SamAccountName), 1 = UPN (User Principal Name), 2 = Email, 3 = SamAccountNameOnly (SamAccountName), 4 = Custom.

requestBody.description:
The settings for the new activity. The id identifies the activity to copy.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): Identifier of the activity. Identifier of the activity to copy. The new activity gets a new id.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the activity. Must be unique among activities, up to 256 characters.
- `description` (string): Description of the activity.
- `platformId` (string (GUID)): Platform the activity applies to. Use the Platform names list to find the id.
- `activityType` (integer): Kind of activity. See the `Values for activityType` paragraph in the operation description.
- `loginAccount` (integer): Type of account the activity signs in with. See the `Values for loginAccount` paragraph in the operation description.
- `loginAccountNameFormat` (string): Template for the sign-in account name, for example one built from %samaccountname%. Not validated on copy.
- `requesterLoginFormat` (integer): Name format to use when the requester is the sign-in account. See the `Values for requesterLoginFormat` paragraph in the operation description.
- `applicationToLaunch` (string): Path of the application to launch for application-launch activities.
- `preferredRDSHostId` (string (GUID)): Resource to use as the preferred Remote Desktop Services host.
- `connectCredentialId` (string (GUID)): Service account used to connect to the Remote Desktop Services host.
- `createAccount` (boolean): Whether to create the account when the session starts. Applies when loginAccount is Managed or Resource.
- `deleteAccount` (boolean): Whether to delete the account when the session ends. When false the account is disabled. Applies when loginAccount is Managed or Resource.
- `vaultId` (string (GUID)): Vault connector used to look up the sign-in credentials. Used when loginAccount is Vault.
- `vaultInfo` (string): Vault-specific settings, as a JSON string. Used when loginAccount is Vault.
- `logonUrl` (string): Sign-in URL for website activities.
- `activityConfigurationId` (string (GUID)): Connection profile settings attached to the activity. If set, the server ignores the id and creates a copy of the original activity's connection profile settings for the new activity. If the original has none, the request fails with 500.
- `startActionGroupId` (string (GUID)): Steps that run when a session starts. Ignored on copy. The server creates a new step group and fills it with copies of the original's steps.
- `duringActionGroupId` (string (GUID)): Steps that run during a session. Ignored on copy. The server creates a new step group and fills it with copies of the original's steps.
- `endActionGroupId` (string (GUID)): Steps that run when a session ends. Ignored on copy. The server creates a new step group and fills it with copies of the original's steps.

201.description: The copy is created. The response body is the new activity, and the Location header points to it.

500.description: The copy could not be created, for example because no activity has the id in the body or the name is already in use.

get.summary: List activity names
get.description:
Returns the id and name of every activity that has not been deleted, sorted by name, including credential release and file release activities. Use it to fill pick lists without loading full activity records.

Permission required: Administrator role. The signed-in session must have completed multifactor authentication.

200.description: An array of objects, each with an id and a name.

delete.description:
Deletes an activity and removes it from every activity group it belongs to. The activity no longer appears in activity lists, and the deletion is recorded in the event log.

Permission required: Administrator role. The signed-in session must have completed multifactor authentication.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the activity.

202.description: The activity is deleted. The response has no body.

400.description: The delete failed. The response body is the error message as plain text.

404.description: No activity exists with this id.

get.summary: Get an activity
get.description:
Returns one activity and its settings. The lookup is by id only, so it also returns deleted activities and credential release and file release activities. Use the activity list if you need group membership and connection profile settings.

Permission required: Administrator role. The signed-in session must have completed multifactor authentication.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the activity.

200.description: The activity.

404.description: No activity exists with this id. The response body is the requested id.

put.description:
Replaces the settings of an existing activity with the activity in the request body. Changes to the name, platform, sign-in account and similar settings are recorded in the event log.

Permission required: Administrator role. The signed-in session must have completed multifactor authentication.

Values for `activityType`: 0 = Interactive, 1 = InteractiveAppLaunch, 2 = TaskAutomation, 3 = CredentialRelease, 4 = FileRelease.

Values for `loginAccount`: 0 = Requester, 1 = Managed, 2 = ActivityIdentity (shown as Activity Token in the console), 3 = Vault, 4 = Resource.

Values for `requesterLoginFormat`: 0 = Samaccountname (Domain\SamAccountName), 1 = UPN (User Principal Name), 2 = Email, 3 = SamAccountNameOnly (SamAccountName), 4 = Custom.

Caution: The change replaces the stored activity and takes effect immediately, so send the full activity rather than only the fields you want to change.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the activity.

requestBody.description:
The complete activity with your changes. The id must match the id in the path.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): Identifier of the activity. Must match the id in the path; otherwise the request fails with 400.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the activity. Must be unique among activities, up to 256 characters.
- `description` (string): Description of the activity.
- `platformId` (string (GUID)): Platform the activity applies to. Use the Platform names list to find the id.
- `activityType` (integer): Kind of activity. See the `Values for activityType` paragraph in the operation description.
- `loginAccount` (integer): Type of account the activity signs in with. See the `Values for loginAccount` paragraph in the operation description.
- `loginAccountNameFormat` (string): Template for the sign-in account name, for example one built from %samaccountname%. Required and validated unless loginAccount is Requester or Vault. An invalid template returns 400 with a message.
- `requesterLoginFormat` (integer): Name format to use when the requester is the sign-in account. See the `Values for requesterLoginFormat` paragraph in the operation description.
- `applicationToLaunch` (string): Path of the application to launch for application-launch activities.
- `preferredRDSHostId` (string (GUID)): Resource to use as the preferred Remote Desktop Services host.
- `connectCredentialId` (string (GUID)): Service account used to connect to the Remote Desktop Services host.
- `createAccount` (boolean): Whether to create the account when the session starts. Applies when loginAccount is Managed or Resource.
- `deleteAccount` (boolean): Whether to delete the account when the session ends. When false the account is disabled. Applies when loginAccount is Managed or Resource.
- `vaultId` (string (GUID)): Vault connector used to look up the sign-in credentials. Used when loginAccount is Vault.
- `vaultInfo` (string): Vault-specific settings, as a JSON string. Used when loginAccount is Vault.
- `logonUrl` (string): Sign-in URL for website activities.
- `activityConfigurationId` (string (GUID)): Connection profile settings attached to the activity.
- `startActionGroupId` (string (GUID)): Steps that run when a session starts. If omitted, null or the empty GUID on create, an empty step group is created and its id is returned. On update, omitted ids keep their current values.
- `duringActionGroupId` (string (GUID)): Steps that run during a session. Same behavior as startActionGroupId.
- `endActionGroupId` (string (GUID)): Steps that run when a session ends. Same behavior as startActionGroupId.

200.description: The activity is updated. The response body is the updated activity.

400.description: The id in the path does not match the id in the body, or the sign-in account name template is missing or invalid. The response body is a message as plain text.

404.description: No activity exists with this id.

500.description: The update failed, for example because another activity already has the same name or the name is missing.

get.summary: Get an activity and its access policies
get.description:
Returns an activity together with the access policies that use it. Use it to see where an activity applies before you change or delete it.

Permission required: Administrator role. The signed-in session must have completed multifactor authentication.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the activity.

200.description: An object with an activity property holding the activity and a policies property holding an array of access policies. If no activity has this id, activity is null and policies is empty.

get.summary: List all activity groups
get.description:
Returns every activity group, including the activities in each group. Groups marked as deleted are not filtered out.

Permission required: Administrator role.

200.description: An array of activity groups.

post.description:
Creates an activity group. If a deleted group has the same id or name, that group is restored with the new description instead of a new one being created.

Permission required: Administrator role.

requestBody.description:
The activity group to create.

- `id` (string (GUID)): Identifier of the activity group. Optional. If a group marked as deleted has this id or this name, that group is restored instead of a new one being created.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the activity group. Must be unique among activity groups, up to 256 characters.
- `description` (string): Description of the activity group.
- `activityGroupActivities` (array of objects): Activities to place in the group when it is created. Each object needs the activityId of an existing activity. Optional. Ignored when a deleted group is restored. If an activityId does not match an activity, the request fails with 500 but the group itself is still created. You can also add activities after creation with the add activities route.

201.description: The group is created or restored. The response body is the activity group, and the Location header points to it.

500.description: The group could not be created, for example because another activity group already has the same name or the name is missing.

get.summary: List activity group names
get.description:
Returns the id and name of every activity group that has not been deleted, sorted by name.

Permission required: Administrator role.

200.description: An array of objects, each with an id and a name.

get.summary: Search the activities in a group
get.description:
Returns a page of the activities that belong to an activity group. You can filter by text and choose the sort order.

Permission required: Administrator role.

parameters.name: activityGroupId
parameters.description: Identifier of the activity group.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of activities to skip. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Maximum number of activities to return. Defaults to 100.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Name of the property to sort by. Defaults to Name.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Return only activities whose name or description contains this text. The match ignores case.

parameters.name: FilterColumns
parameters.description: Accepted but not used by this route. The text filter always searches a fixed set of columns.

200.description: An object with a data array of activities and a recordsTotal count of all matches.

400.description: The search failed. The response body is a message.

404.description: No activity group exists with this id. The response body is a message.

delete.description:
Deletes an activity group permanently, together with its activity memberships. The activities in the group are not deleted.

Permission required: Administrator role.

Caution: The group is removed permanently and cannot be restored. Check which access policies use it first with the get activity group and access policies route.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the activity group.

202.description: The deletion is accepted. The response has no body. An id that does not match a group also returns 202.

get.summary: Get an activity group
get.description:
Returns one activity group, including the activities in it. A group marked as deleted is still returned.

Permission required: Administrator role.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the activity group.

200.description: The activity group.

404.description: No activity group exists with this id.

put.description:
Changes the name and description of an activity group. Other properties in the request body are ignored; use the add and remove activities routes to change membership.

Permission required: Administrator role.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the activity group.

requestBody.description:
The activity group. Only name and description can be changed on update.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): Identifier of the activity group. Must match the id in the path; otherwise the request fails with 400.

post.summary: Create and start an activity session
post.description:
Creates an activity session for the target resource or credential and queues it to start. If the access policy requires approval, the session waits for approval before it is scheduled. The session is created for the signed-in user, and application accounts must name the user in managedAccountId.

Permission required: Any signed-in user with a managed account, or an application account.

Values for `customFields[].customFieldDataType`: 0 = Integer, 1 = String, 2 = Options.

requestBody.description:
The session to create. Identify the target with a resource or a credential field and the activity with activityName or activityId.

- `managedResourceId` (string (uuid)): Identifier of the resource to connect to. Provide the resource or a credential, unless the activity only assigns group roles, which needs neither. The server checks managedResourceId first, then managedResourceName, then credentialId, then credentialUsername with credentialDomain, then credentialName, and uses the first one present. An identifier that is really a credential is accepted.
- `managedResourceName` (string): DNS host name of the resource to connect to. Used when managedResourceId is not sent.
- `credentialId` (string (uuid)): Identifier of the credential to release, for a credential session.
- `credentialUsername` (string): User name of the credential to release. Send together with credentialDomain.
- `credentialDomain` (string): Domain or host name of the credential to release. Empty for Entra ID accounts.
- `credentialName` (string): Name of the credential to release.
- `activityName` (string): Name of the activity to run, for example Credential Release. When set, it is looked up by exact name and replaces activityId. Send activityName or activityId; one of them is required.
- `activityId` (string (uuid)): Identifier of the activity to run. Send this or activityName; one of them is required.
- `accessPolicyId` (string (uuid)): Identifier of the access policy that grants the session.
- `startDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): UTC time the session starts. A future time schedules the session. If left empty or set in the past, the session starts now.
- `endDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): UTC time the session ends. If left out or earlier than the start, the session ends after the maximum session length of its connection profile. A later time is capped to that maximum.
- `note` (string): A note to store with the session. Required when the access policy requires notes.
- `ticket` (string): A ticket reference to store with the session. Required when the access policy requires a ticket.
- `managedAccountId` (string (uuid)): Identifier of the user the session is created for. Application accounts must send it. Used only for application accounts. For every other caller the server replaces it with the caller's own account.
- `encryptedFileId` (string (uuid)): Identifier of the encrypted file to release, for a file release session.
- `customFields` (array of objects): Values for custom fields on the access policy. Each item has policyId, name, value and customFieldDataType. Send customFieldDataType as a number, see the enum notes.
- `runtimeParameterOverrides` (array of objects): Values that replace action parameters for this session. Each item has actionId, parameterName and value.

201.description: The session was created and queued. The body is the new activity session, and the Location header points to it.

400.description: The request is not valid. The body is the message, for example that the account is locked, that the resource, credential or activity could not be found, that no resource or credential was supplied, that no access policy grants the user this activity, or that a note or ticket the policy requires is missing.

401.description: The request is not signed in, or the sign-in has expired.

404.description: The account for the session was not found.

post.summary: Create a group of activity sessions

Creates one or more activity sessions together as a group and queues them to start. All sessions are created for the signed-in user. This is the route the console uses when a user requests a session. Sessions are created one at a time, so if a later request in the array fails, the sessions created before it remain.

Permission required: Any signed-in user with a managed account.
