requestBody.description:
A JSON array with one session request for each session to create. Each item has the same fields as the request to create a single session, except that managedAccountId is ignored.

- `(array item)` (array of objects, required): One session request per item. At least one item is required. Fields: managedResourceId, managedResourceName, credentialId, credentialUsername, credentialDomain, credentialName, activityName, activityId, accessPolicyId, startDateTimeUtc, endDateTimeUtc, note, ticket, encryptedFileId, customFields, runtimeParameterOverrides. See POST /api/v1/ActivitySession for what each field does. Send customFieldDataType inside customFields as a number, see the enum notes.

201.description: The group and its sessions were created and queued. The body is the group, with its sessions in activitySessions.

400.description: The array is empty, the account or resources are locked, a resource, credential or activity could not be found, no access policy grants the user an activity, or a note or ticket the policy requires is missing. The body is the message.

401.description: The request is not signed in, or the sign-in has expired.

403.description: The signed-in account is not linked to a managed account.

404.description: The account for the sessions was not found.

put.summary: Lock or unlock live activity sessions
put.description:
Locks or unlocks one or more activity sessions. A locked session shows a message to the user until it is unlocked. You can also lock the user, or the user on one resource, so that new sessions are blocked too.

Permission required: Administrators and application accounts. An auditor needs a role that includes auditor permissions, and an auditor or an administrator in read-only view also needs the Lock Session permission for each session's user and resource.

Caution: Locking or unlocking takes effect immediately, and locking the user affects all of that user's active and pending sessions until you unlock them. Unlocking is not limited to the sessions you list. Sessions are processed in order, so if one fails, the sessions before it have already been changed.

requestBody.description:
The sessions to lock or unlock and how.

- `activitySessionIds` (array of strings (uuid), required): Identifiers of the sessions to lock or unlock. At least one is required.
- `locked` (boolean, required): True to lock the sessions, false to unlock them. If left out it is treated as false and the sessions are unlocked. Unlocking removes the user's block on the session's resource, unlocks the user's account, and unlocks all of that user's active, pending and approval-required sessions, whatever the other flags say.
- `lockResource` (boolean): When locking, also block this user from starting new sessions on the session's resource.
- `lockUser` (boolean): When locking, also lock the user: all of the user's active, pending and approval-required sessions are locked and new sessions are blocked.
- `lockActivity` (boolean): Not used by this route. The session itself is locked whenever locked is true.
- `lockMessage` (string): Message shown to the user. Defaults to a message asking them to contact a Netwrix Privilege Secure administrator.
- `lockTitle` (string): Title of the message dialog. Defaults to Netwrix Privilege Secure.
- `id` (string (uuid)): Not needed for this request. You can leave it out.

200.description: The lock or unlock was applied. The body repeats the request.

400.description: No session identifiers were supplied, or an identifier was empty. The body is the error message.

401.description: The request is not signed in, or the sign-in has expired.

403.description: The caller is not allowed to lock these sessions, for example an auditor without the Lock Session permission.

404.description: One of the sessions was not found.

post.description:
Adds time to an activity session and returns the updated session. The session's connection profile must allow extensions, extensions must remain, and the requested time cannot exceed the length allowed for one extension. If the body is left out or the number is zero or negative, the full allowed extension is added.

Permission required: Administrators and application accounts, or the user who owns the session.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the activity session.

requestBody.description:
The number of minutes to add, sent as a single JSON integer.

- `(request body)` (integer): Minutes to add to the session. Zero, a negative number or no body adds the full allowed extension. Send as a bare number, for example 120.

200.description: The session was extended. The body is the updated activity session.

400.description: The session cannot be extended, for example because extensions are not allowed, none remain, or the time is too long. The body is the error message.

401.description: The request is not signed in, or the sign-in has expired.

404.description: No activity session exists with this identifier.

500.description: The caller is not an administrator, an application account or the session owner. The server fails the request instead of returning 403.

get.summary: Get the log of an activity session
get.description:
Returns the log lines recorded for one activity session, limited to the time window of the session. Use it to see what the session did and whether any step failed.

Permission required: Administrators, application accounts, Auditing and Reporting role, the session owner, or an auditor allowed to audit this session.

Values for `logLevel (and status on each line)`: 0 = Debug, 1 = Info, 2 = Warn, 3 = Error.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the activity session.

parameters.name: logLevel
parameters.description: Lowest log level to return. Send the number. 0 returns every line.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of log lines to skip. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Number of log lines to return. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to return the newest lines first. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Return only lines that contain this text.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Return lines from this UTC date and time. It can only narrow the session's own time window.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Return lines up to this UTC date and time. It can only narrow the session's own time window.

200.description: The log lines in lines, with totalCount for the full match count.

400.description: No session identifier was provided, the auditor is not allowed to view this session's logs, or the request failed. The body is the error message.

401.description: The request is not signed in, or the sign-in has expired.

403.description: The caller is not allowed to view this session's logs.

404.description: No activity session exists with this identifier.

get.summary: Get the password for an active credential session
get.description:
Returns the password of the credential that belongs to an active session so the owner can copy it. It is returned as plain text, or as a JSON string when the request accepts JSON.

Permission required: Only the user who owns the session, and only when the session's connection profile allows password access.

Caution: The response contains a password in clear text, and each request is recorded in the audit log.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the activity session.

200.description: The password.

400.description: The request failed. The body is the error message.

401.description: The request is not signed in, or the sign-in has expired.

404.description: The caller does not own the session, the session is not active, the connection profile does not allow password access, the session has no credential, or no password is stored.

get.summary: List Active Directory domain configurations
get.description:
Returns every configured Active Directory domain, including the service account each domain uses and whether it connects over SSL. Use it to list the domains the product can work with.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

200.description: The list of domain configurations.

get.summary: List domain names and IDs
get.description:
Returns the name and ID of each configured Active Directory domain, sorted by name. Use it to fill a domain picker without loading full configurations.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

200.description: A list of domain names and IDs.

delete.summary: Delete an Active Directory domain configuration
delete.description:
Removes the domain configuration and the resource that represents the domain, marks the stored credentials of the domain's accounts and resources as deleted, and removes the domain's managed resources and its scheduled domain sync job. The call is refused if resource groups still depend on the domain, or if you are signed in as an administrator with an account from that same domain.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the domain configuration to delete.

200.description: The domain configuration was deleted. The body is the JSON string "Ok".

400.description: The domain cannot be deleted, for example because resource groups depend on it, your own account belongs to it, or no domain configuration has that ID.

get.summary: Get a domain configuration by ID or name
get.description:
Returns the configuration of the Active Directory domain with the given ID or domain name. The path value is either the ID of the domain configuration or the name of the domain.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the domain configuration, or the name of the domain.

200.description: The domain configuration.

404.description: No domain configuration has that ID or domain name.

get.summary: List approval workflows
get.description:
Returns all approval workflows, each with its tiers and approvers. Use it to see which approval processes are defined.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Values for `progressionType (on each tier)`: 0 = Sequential, 1 = Concurrent.

200.description: The list of approval workflows.

400.description: The request failed.

post.description:
Creates an approval workflow with its tiers, approvers and approver groups. Use it to define who must approve access requests and in what order.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Values for `progressionType (on each tier)`: 0 = Sequential, 1 = Concurrent.

Caution: The workflow is saved before the response is built, so an error response does not always mean that nothing was created. Check the workflow list before you retry. The console and other clients save workflows with PUT; prefer PUT for a reliable result.

requestBody.description:
The workflow to create, with its tiers.

- `id` (string (GUID)): ID of the workflow. Leave empty or omit when creating; the server assigns it.
- `nodeId` (string (GUID)): Server node the record belongs to. Set by the server.
- `approvalWorkflowTiers` (array of tier objects): The tiers of the workflow in order. Each tier has tierNumber, progressionType (0 Sequential, 1 Concurrent), requiredApprovalCount, escalationTimeout, an optional escalation approver account or group, and its approvers and approver groups. Defaults to an empty list.
- `modifiedBy` (string (GUID)): User who last changed the workflow. Set by the server.
- `modifiedDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Time of the last change. Set by the server.
- `createdDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Time the workflow was created. Set by the server.

201.description: The workflow was created and is returned.

400.description: The workflow could not be created; the body holds the reason.

500.description: The workflow was saved but the server could not build the response. Check the workflow list before you retry.

put.description:
Saves an approval workflow with its tiers and approvers. The tiers you send replace the stored ones: tiers left out of the request are deleted, and each tier's approvers and approver groups are replaced by the ones you send. If no workflow with the given ID exists, a new one is created.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Values for `progressionType (on each tier)`: 0 = Sequential, 1 = Concurrent.

Caution: The change takes effect immediately, and any tier you leave out of the request is deleted.

requestBody.description:
The full workflow as it should be saved.

- `id` (string (GUID)): ID of the workflow to update. If no workflow has this ID, a new workflow is created.
- `nodeId` (string (GUID)): Server node the record belongs to. Set by the server.
- `approvalWorkflowTiers` (array of tier objects): The tiers of the workflow in order. Each tier has tierNumber, progressionType (0 Sequential, 1 Concurrent), requiredApprovalCount, escalationTimeout, an optional escalation approver account or group, and its approvers and approver groups. When the workflow already exists, tiers are renumbered 1, 2, 3 in the order of their tierNumber values. Send every tier you want to keep, with its id; a tier without an id is added as a new tier.
- `modifiedBy` (string (GUID)): User who last changed the workflow. Set by the server.
- `modifiedDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Time of the last change. Set by the server.
- `createdDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Time the workflow was created. Set by the server.

200.description: The saved workflow is returned.

400.description: The workflow could not be saved; the body holds the reason.

get.summary: List approvals for an activity session
get.description:
Returns the approval records for the given activity session across all tiers, showing who must approve and the state of each approval.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Values for `approvalState`: 0 = Pending, 1 = Approved, 2 = Denied.

Values for `approverType`: 0 = Normal, 1 = Escalated, 2 = Requester.

parameters.name: activitySessionId
parameters.description: ID of the activity session.

200.description: The list of approvals, which is empty when there are none.

400.description: The request failed.

put.summary: Approve or deny an access request
put.description:
Records an approver's decision and notes on every approval that approver holds for an activity session. The approval process then advances: a completed tier moves the workflow on, and if the combined result of the workflow becomes Denied, the approval process for the session is cancelled.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Values for `approvalState`: 0 = Pending, 1 = Approved, 2 = Denied.

Caution: The decision takes effect immediately; if it makes the combined result Denied, the approval process for the session is cancelled.

requestBody.description:
The approver's decision for the session.

- `approverAccountId` (string (GUID), required): ID of the approver account.
- `activitySessionId` (string (GUID), required): ID of the activity session being decided.
- `approvalState` (integer, required): The decision: 1 to approve, 2 to deny. 0 is Pending.
- `approverNotes` (string): Notes from the approver.

200.description: The decision was recorded. The call also returns 200 and changes nothing when the approver has no approvals for that session.

400.description: The decision could not be recorded; the body holds the reason.

delete.description:
Deletes a single approval record from an approval workflow. The record is removed immediately; the call also returns 202 when no approval has that ID.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the approval to delete.

202.description: The approval was deleted, or no approval had that ID.

400.description: The approval could not be deleted; the body holds the reason.

get.summary: Get an approval by ID
get.description:
Returns one approval record, including its state and any notes from the approver.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Values for `approvalState`: 0 = Pending, 1 = Approved, 2 = Denied.

Values for `approverType`: 0 = Normal, 1 = Escalated, 2 = Requester.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the approval.

200.description: The approval.

400.description: The request failed.

404.description: No approval has that ID.

get.summary: Search accounts and groups that can approve in a tier
get.description:
Searches the accounts and groups that can be added as approvers to an approval tier, with paging, sorting and text filtering. Accounts and groups already assigned to the tier are left out, and applications and collections are never returned. Use it to populate an approver picker.

Permission required: Administrator role.

Values for `entityType`: 0 = ManagedAccount, 1 = ManagedAccountGroup, 4 = Local.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the approval tier to find candidates for. Required in practice; an empty value returns 400.

parameters.name: entityType
parameters.description: Limits results to one type of approver. Send the name or the number: ManagedAccount (0), ManagedAccountGroup (1) or Local (4).

parameters.name: Skip
parameters.description: Number of items to skip. Default 0.

parameters.name: Take
parameters.description: Number of items to return. Default 100.

parameters.name: OrderBy
parameters.description: Name of the property to sort by. By default results are sorted by display name.

parameters.name: OrderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. Default false.

parameters.name: FilterText
parameters.description: Returns only entries whose name, display name, domain, email, SAM account name or user principal name contains this text (case-insensitive).

parameters.name: FilterColumns
parameters.description: Accepted but has no effect on this route; the text filter always searches the fields listed for FilterText.

200.description: A page of candidate approvers. The body has data (the page of rows) and recordsTotal (the number of matching rows before paging is applied).

400.description: No tier ID was provided, or the search failed.

get.summary: Get the approval tier for an approval
get.description:
Returns the approval tier that an approval record belongs to. Use it when you have an approval ID and need the tier it is part of.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Values for `progressionType`: 0 = Sequential, 1 = Concurrent.

parameters.name: workflowApprovalId
parameters.description: ID of the approval.

200.description: The approval tier.

204.description: No tier was found for that approval.

400.description: The request failed.

get.summary: Get an approval tier by ID
get.description:
Returns an approval tier, including its approvers, approver groups and escalation settings. Send the tier ID in the id query parameter; the value in the path is not used.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Values for `progressionType`: 0 = Sequential, 1 = Concurrent.

Caution: The tier can include approver account details, which may be sensitive.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Any value. The route needs a path segment here, but the value is not used.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the approval tier. This is the value the server uses.

200.description: The approval tier.

204.description: No tier was found for that ID.

400.description: The request failed.

get.summary: List a tier's approvals for an activity session
get.description:
Returns the approval records for one approval tier in the given activity session.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Values for `approvalState`: 0 = Pending, 1 = Approved, 2 = Denied.

Values for `approverType`: 0 = Normal, 1 = Escalated, 2 = Requester.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the approval tier.

parameters.name: activitySessionId
parameters.description: ID of the activity session.

200.description: The list of approvals, which is empty when there are none.

400.description: The request failed.

get.summary: Get the approval workflow for a tier
get.description:
Returns the approval workflow that contains the given tier.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

parameters.name: workflowTierId
parameters.description: ID of the approval tier.

200.description: The approval workflow.

204.description: No workflow was found for that tier.

400.description: The request failed.

delete.description:
Deletes an approval workflow. The workflow is removed immediately; the call also returns 202 when no workflow has that ID.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the approval workflow to delete.

202.description: The workflow was deleted, or no workflow had that ID.

400.description: The workflow could not be deleted; the body holds the reason.

get.summary: Get an approval workflow by ID
get.description:
Returns one approval workflow with its tiers, approvers and approver groups.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Values for `progressionType (on each tier)`: 0 = Sequential, 1 = Concurrent.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the approval workflow.

200.description: The approval workflow.

400.description: The request failed.

404.description: No workflow has that ID.

get.summary: Get the approval state of a session
get.description:
Returns the overall approval result for an activity session under the given workflow: Pending, Approved or Denied.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Values for the response: 0 = Pending, 1 = Approved, 2 = Denied.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the approval workflow.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: ID of the activity session.

200.description: The approval state.

400.description: The request failed.

404.description: No workflow has that ID.

get.summary: List the record types that appear in the change audit
get.description:
Returns the record types (each with a name and a display title) that appear in the change audit log. Use it to fill a filter list before you call the change audit search. The result is wrapped in an object that holds the list in a data array and the number of entries in recordsTotal.

Permission required: Administrator or Auditing and Reporting role.

200.description: The list of record types, wrapped in an object with data and recordsTotal.

post.description:
Creates an Entra ID tenant configuration and returns it with its new ID. Creating the tenant also adds a virtual host, a resource and a website that represent it, so you can manage the tenant like other resources. If any of these cannot be created, everything created so far is removed and the call returns 400.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Caution: The tenant is created immediately.

requestBody.description:
The tenant to create.

- `id` (string (GUID)): ID of the tenant configuration. Leave out on create.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the tenant in the console.
- `description` (string): Description of the tenant. Not saved on create. Set it with an update.
- `tenantId` (string, required): The Microsoft Entra directory (tenant) ID.
- `emailDomain` (string, required): The tenant's email domain, for example the onmicrosoft.com domain. Required: the create fails without it.
- `logonUrl` (string, required): The sign-in URL for the tenant portal.
- `platformId` (string (GUID)): ID of the platform the tenant belongs to. Not used on create: a new tenant always uses the Entra ID platform. You can change it later with an update.
- `serviceAccountId` (string (GUID)): ID of the service account the product uses to manage the tenant. Can be left out; set it so the product has an account to manage the tenant with.
- `processGroupMembership` (boolean): Whether group membership is processed for the tenant. Not saved on create. Set it with an update.
- `associatedDomainId` (string (GUID)): ID of an associated Active Directory domain.
- `managedResourceId` (string (GUID)): ID of the resource that represents the tenant. The product sets it.
- `virtualHostId` (string (GUID)): ID of the virtual host for the tenant. The product sets it.
- `virtualWebsiteId` (string (GUID)): ID of the virtual website for the tenant. The product sets it.

200.description: The tenant was created. The body is the new tenant configuration.

400.description: The tenant could not be created. The body is an error message as a JSON string.

delete.description:
Deletes the Entra ID tenant configuration with the given ID, along with the resource and website that represent it, and returns the ID of the deleted tenant. Use it to stop managing a tenant.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Caution: The tenant is deleted immediately.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: ID of the Entra ID tenant configuration.

200.description: The tenant was deleted. The body is the tenant ID.

400.description: The tenant could not be deleted. The body is an error message as a JSON string.

404.description: The tenant was not found, or it has no resource record.

get.summary: Get an Entra ID tenant
get.description:
Returns the settings of one Entra ID tenant configuration, identified by its ID.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: ID of the Entra ID tenant configuration.

200.description: The tenant configuration.

404.description: The tenant was not found, or it has no resource record.

get.summary: List Entra ID tenants
get.description:
Returns all configured Entra ID tenants. The list is empty when none are configured.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

200.description: An array of tenant configurations.

400.description: The tenant list could not be retrieved. The body is the message "Unable to retrieve Entra ID Tenant list."

get.summary: Get the Entra ID tenant for a virtual host
get.description:
Returns the Entra ID tenant configuration that is linked to the given virtual host. Use it when you have the virtual host ID and need the tenant it belongs to.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

parameters.name: virtualHostId
parameters.description: ID of the virtual host linked to the tenant.

200.description: The tenant configuration.

404.description: No tenant is linked to that virtual host.

put.description:
Replaces the settings of an existing Entra ID tenant configuration and returns the updated tenant. The id in the request body must match the tenantId in the URL. Changing the name also renames the tenant's virtual host and website.

Permission required: Administrator or application role.

Caution: The change takes effect immediately.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: ID of the Entra ID tenant configuration.

requestBody.description:
The full tenant configuration to save.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): ID of the tenant configuration. Must match the tenantId in the URL; otherwise the call returns 400.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the tenant in the console.
- `description` (string): Description of the tenant.
- `tenantId` (string, required): The Microsoft Entra directory (tenant) ID.
- `emailDomain` (string, required): The tenant's email domain, for example the onmicrosoft.com domain.
- `logonUrl` (string, required): The sign-in URL for the tenant portal.
- `platformId` (string (GUID), required): ID of the platform the tenant belongs to. Changing it moves the tenant's resource to that platform.
- `serviceAccountId` (string (GUID)): ID of the service account the product uses to manage the tenant. Leaving it out clears the service account for the tenant.
- `processGroupMembership` (boolean): Whether group membership is processed for the tenant.
- `associatedDomainId` (string (GUID)): ID of an associated Active Directory domain.
- `managedResourceId` (string (GUID)): ID of the resource that represents the tenant. The product sets it. Ignored on update.
- `virtualHostId` (string (GUID)): ID of the virtual host for the tenant. The product sets it. Ignored on update.
- `virtualWebsiteId` (string (GUID)): ID of the virtual website for the tenant. The product sets it. Ignored on update.

200.description: The tenant was updated. The body is the updated tenant configuration.

400.description: The tenant could not be updated, for example because the IDs do not match.

404.description: The tenant was not found.

post.description:
Creates a command restriction and returns it. Use it to define keywords for commands that sessions log, block, lock or terminate, and who is notified.

Permission required: Administrator who has completed multi-factor authentication.

Values for `commandRestrictionSettings[].commandRestrictionMatchType`: 0 = Keyword.

Values for `commandRestrictionSettings[].commandRestrictionActionType`: 0 = LogOnly, 1 = Block, 2 = BlockAndLock, 3 = Terminate.

Caution: The command restriction is created immediately.

requestBody.description:
The command restriction to create.

- `id` (string (GUID)): ID of the command restriction. Leave out on create.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the command restriction, up to 256 characters.
- `emailRecipient` (string (email)): Email address to notify. Leave the field out if you have no address. An empty string is rejected with a 400.
- `commandRestrictionSettings` (array): The settings that define which commands are matched and what happens. Each item has commandRestrictionSettingNumber, active, email, emailRecipient, lockMessage, match, commandRestrictionMatchType and commandRestrictionActionType. See the enum values.

200.description: The command restriction was created. The body is the new command restriction.

400.description: The command restriction could not be created, for example because the request is not valid.

put.description:
Updates an existing command restriction, identified by the id in the request body, and returns the saved result. The settings in the request replace the existing settings.

Permission required: Administrator who has completed multi-factor authentication.

Values for `commandRestrictionSettings[].commandRestrictionMatchType`: 0 = Keyword.

Values for `commandRestrictionSettings[].commandRestrictionActionType`: 0 = LogOnly, 1 = Block, 2 = BlockAndLock, 3 = Terminate.

Caution: The change takes effect immediately.

requestBody.description:
The command restriction to save, including its id.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): ID of the command restriction. Required on update; the call returns 404 if no command restriction has this ID.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the command restriction, up to 256 characters.
- `emailRecipient` (string (email)): Email address to notify. Leave the field out if you have no address. An empty string is rejected with a 400.
- `commandRestrictionSettings` (array): The settings that define which commands are matched and what happens. Send the full list. Settings with an existing id are updated, settings without one are added, and existing settings left out of the list are removed; leaving the field out removes all settings. Each item has commandRestrictionSettingNumber, active, email, emailRecipient, lockMessage, match, commandRestrictionMatchType and commandRestrictionActionType.

200.description: The command restriction was updated. The body is the saved command restriction.

400.description: The command restriction could not be updated.

404.description: The command restriction was not found.

get.summary: List command restriction names and IDs
get.description:
Returns the name and ID of every command restriction, sorted by name. Use it to fill a pick list or to find the ID you need for other calls.

Permission required: Administrator who has completed multi-factor authentication.

200.description: An array of objects with the id and name of each command restriction.

400.description: The list could not be retrieved.

delete.description:
Deletes the command restriction with the given ID, together with its settings. Use it when you no longer need the set of blocked or logged commands.

Permission required: Administrator who has completed multi-factor authentication.

Caution: The command restriction and its settings are deleted immediately. Connection profiles that use it no longer reference any command restriction.

parameters.name: commandRestrictionId
parameters.description: ID of the command restriction.

202.description: The command restriction was deleted. The response has no body.

400.description: The command restriction could not be deleted.

404.description: The command restriction was not found.

get.summary: Get a command restriction
get.description:
Returns one command restriction, including its list of settings that define which commands are matched and what happens when one is used.

Permission required: Administrator who has completed multi-factor authentication.

Values for `commandRestrictionSettings[].commandRestrictionMatchType`: 0 = Keyword.

Values for `commandRestrictionSettings[].commandRestrictionActionType`: 0 = LogOnly, 1 = Block, 2 = BlockAndLock, 3 = Terminate.

parameters.name: commandRestrictionId
parameters.description: ID of the command restriction.

200.description: The command restriction and its settings.

400.description: The command restriction could not be retrieved.

404.description: The command restriction was not found.

get.summary: List connection profiles
get.description:
Returns all connection profiles. Use it to choose a profile when you create or edit an access policy. The list also includes a default connection profile that was deleted, because the default profile is only marked as deleted; check its isDeleted field. Reading a profile that has no approval workflow creates an empty one, and reading a profile that has no approval email template assigns the default template; either way the profile is saved.

Permission required: Administrator, or a user with the User Plus role and the Access Policies permission.

Values for `type`: 0 = Generic, 1 = ConnectionProfile, 2 = EmailSettings, 3 = System.

Values for `approvalTypeRequired`: 0 = Deny, 1 = Allow, 2 = Workflow, 3 = External.

Values for `activityConfigurationSettings[].type`: 0 = String, 1 = Integer, 2 = UnsignedInteger, 3 = Boolean, 4 = Guid.

200.description: An array of connection profiles.

400.description: The list could not be retrieved.

post.description:
Creates a connection profile and returns it. The name must not match another connection profile.

Permission required: Administrator.

Values for `type`: 0 = Generic, 1 = ConnectionProfile, 2 = EmailSettings, 3 = System.

Values for `approvalTypeRequired`: 0 = Deny, 1 = Allow, 2 = Workflow, 3 = External.

Values for `activityConfigurationSettings[].type`: 0 = String, 1 = Integer, 2 = UnsignedInteger, 3 = Boolean, 4 = Guid.

Values for `customFields[].customFieldDataType`: 0 = Integer, 1 = String, 2 = Options.

Caution: The profile is created immediately.

requestBody.description:
The connection profile to create. Only the main fields are listed; a profile returned by the get route shows every setting you can send.

- `id` (string (GUID)): ID of the connection profile. Leave out on create.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the profile. It must not match another connection profile's name (case-insensitive).
- `description` (string): Description of the profile.
- `type` (integer): Kind of configuration. Defaults to 0 (Generic) when left out. Send 1 (ConnectionProfile) so that the profile appears in the connection profile list.
- `approvalTypeRequired` (integer): How activity is approved: deny, allow, workflow or external.
- `maxSessionLength` (integer): Maximum session length.
- `allowSessionExtension` (boolean): Whether users can extend a session.
- `record` (boolean): Whether sessions are recorded.
- `notesRequired` (boolean): Whether users must enter notes to start a session.
- `ticketRequired` (boolean): Whether users must enter a ticket to start a session.
- `commandRestrictionId` (string (GUID)): ID of a command restriction to apply.
- `customFields` (array): Custom fields for the profile. Each item has name, label, description, customFieldNumber, customFieldDataType, options and required. See the enum values.
- `activityConfigurationSettings` (array): Additional settings, each with a key, name, value and type.

200.description: The profile was created. The body is the new connection profile.

400.description: The profile could not be created, for example because the name is already used.

get.summary: List connection profile names and IDs
get.description:
Returns the name and ID of every connection profile that has not been deleted, sorted by name.

Permission required: Administrator.

200.description: An array of objects with the id and name of each connection profile.

delete.description:
Deletes a connection profile and returns the deleted profile. The default connection profile is marked as deleted rather than removed, and a profile that access policies use cannot be deleted.

Permission required: Administrator.

Caution: The profile is deleted immediately.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the connection profile.

200.description: The connection profile was deleted. The body is the deleted profile.

400.description: The profile cannot be deleted, for example because access policies use it.

404.description: The connection profile was not found.

get.summary: Get a connection profile
get.description:
Returns the full settings of one connection profile, including its custom fields. Reading a profile that has no approval workflow creates an empty one, and reading a profile that has no approval email template assigns the default template; either way the profile is saved.

Permission required: Administrator.

Values for `type`: 0 = Generic, 1 = ConnectionProfile, 2 = EmailSettings, 3 = System.

Values for `approvalTypeRequired`: 0 = Deny, 1 = Allow, 2 = Workflow, 3 = External.

Values for `activityConfigurationSettings[].type`: 0 = String, 1 = Integer, 2 = UnsignedInteger, 3 = Boolean, 4 = Guid.

Values for `customFields[].customFieldDataType`: 0 = Integer, 1 = String, 2 = Options.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the connection profile.

200.description: The connection profile.

400.description: The profile could not be retrieved.

404.description: The connection profile was not found.

put.description:
Replaces the settings of a connection profile and returns the saved profile. Get the profile first, change the fields you need and send the whole object back. The name must not match another profile.

Permission required: Administrator.

Values for `type`: 0 = Generic, 1 = ConnectionProfile, 2 = EmailSettings, 3 = System.

Values for `approvalTypeRequired`: 0 = Deny, 1 = Allow, 2 = Workflow, 3 = External.

Values for `activityConfigurationSettings[].type`: 0 = String, 1 = Integer, 2 = UnsignedInteger, 3 = Boolean, 4 = Guid.

Values for `customFields[].customFieldDataType`: 0 = Integer, 1 = String, 2 = Options.

Caution: The change takes effect immediately and applies to access policies that use the profile.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the connection profile.

requestBody.description:
The full connection profile to save. Only the main fields are listed; a profile returned by the get route shows every setting you can send.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): ID of the connection profile. Use the same ID as in the URL; the route does not check that the two match. The profile and its custom fields are saved under this id, but custom fields missing from the list are removed from the profile the URL names.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the profile. It must not match another connection profile's name (case-insensitive).
- `description` (string): Description of the profile.
- `type` (integer, required): Kind of configuration. Send 1 (ConnectionProfile). Other values create a configuration that does not appear in the connection profile list.
- `approvalTypeRequired` (integer): How activity is approved: deny, allow, workflow or external.
- `maxSessionLength` (integer): Maximum session length.
- `allowSessionExtension` (boolean): Whether users can extend a session.
- `record` (boolean): Whether sessions are recorded.
- `notesRequired` (boolean): Whether users must enter notes to start a session.
- `ticketRequired` (boolean): Whether users must enter a ticket to start a session.
- `commandRestrictionId` (string (GUID)): ID of a command restriction to apply.
- `customFields` (array): Custom fields for the profile. Send the full list. Custom fields left out of the list (matched by name) are removed; leaving the field out removes all custom fields. Each item has name, label, description, customFieldNumber, customFieldDataType, options and required. See the enum values.
- `activityConfigurationSettings` (array): Additional settings, each with a key, name, value and type.

GET the profile, change one field such as maxSessionLength, send the whole object back.

200.description: The profile was updated. The body is the saved connection profile.

400.description: The profile could not be updated, for example because the name is already used.

get.summary: List groups with console administrator access
get.description:
Returns the Active Directory groups whose members have administrator access to the console.

Permission required: Administrator role or an application (API) token.

200.description: An array of Active Directory groups.

delete.summary: Remove console administrator access from a group
delete.description:
Removes the specified Active Directory group from the list of groups whose members have administrator access to the console. Use it to revoke access previously granted to a whole group.

Permission required: Administrator role or an application (API) token.

Caution: The change takes effect immediately and removes console administrator access for every member of the group who does not have access another way.

parameters.name: adGroupId
parameters.description: ID of the Active Directory group to remove.

200.description: Access was removed, or the group had no access. The response has no body.

404.description: No Active Directory group exists with the supplied ID.

put.summary: Give a group console administrator access
put.description:
Grants administrator access to the console to all members of the specified Active Directory group. The call takes no request body.

Permission required: Administrator role or an application (API) token.

Caution: The change takes effect immediately and grants console administrator access to every member of the group.

parameters.name: adGroupId
parameters.description: ID of the Active Directory group to grant access to.

200.description: Access was granted, or the entry already had it. The response has no body.

404.description: No Active Directory group exists with the supplied ID.

post.summary: Remove console administrator access from several entries
post.description:
Removes console administrator access for each listed entry in one call and returns a pass and fail report. Each entry is processed independently. You cannot remove your own entry or a group or collection you belong to, and an ID that matches no administrator entry is also rejected; these are reported as failures.

Permission required: Administrator role.

Caution: The change takes effect immediately and revokes console administrator access for every listed entry.

requestBody.description:
A JSON array of administrator entry IDs, as returned in the id field of the administrator search results.

- `(array item)` (string (GUID), required): ID of an administrator entry to remove. This is the entry ID from the administrator search, not the user's account ID. Send the body as a bare JSON array of IDs.

200.description: A report with passed and failed counts and a report array with one message per entry. The status is 200 even when some or all entries failed, so check the failed count.

404.description: The signed-in account could not be identified.

get.summary: Search users and groups with console administrator access
get.description:
Returns a page of the users, groups, applications and collections that currently have administrator access to the console, with optional filtering by type and text. Use it to list administrators or to find entry IDs for the remove-multiple call.

Permission required: Administrator role.

Values for `filterEntityType`: 0 = ManagedAccount, 1 = ManagedAccountGroup, 2 = Application, 3 = Collection, 4 = Local.

Values for `entityType`: 0 = ManagedAccount, 1 = ManagedAccountGroup, 2 = Application, 3 = Collection, 4 = Local.

parameters.name: filterEntityType
parameters.description: Limits results to one entry type. Send the number from the entry type list. Omit to include every type.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Text to match, ignoring case, against the entry name, user name or email address. Omit to skip text filtering.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Name of an entry field to sort by, such as name. The match ignores case. Results are also sorted by name after this field. An unrecognized field name falls back to sorting by name only, and none turns sorting off. The default is name.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. The default is false.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of entries to skip, used for paging. The default is 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return. The default is 100.

200.description: An object with a data array of administrator entries and recordsTotal, the total number of matching entries. The id of each entry identifies the administrator entry, not the underlying account, and is the value to pass to the remove-multiple call.

get.summary: Search users and groups eligible for console administrator access
get.description:
Returns a page of the users, applications, groups and collections that can be given administrator access to the console, with optional filtering by type and text. Entries that already have access are not listed. Use it to find entries to pass to the add-multiple call.

Permission required: Administrator role.

Values for `filterEntityType`: 0 = ManagedAccount, 1 = ManagedAccountGroup, 2 = Application, 3 = Collection, 4 = Local.

Values for `entityType`: 0 = ManagedAccount, 1 = ManagedAccountGroup, 2 = Application, 3 = Collection, 4 = Local.

parameters.name: filterEntityType
parameters.description: Limits results to one entry type. Send the number from the entry type list. Omit to include every type.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Text to match, ignoring case, against the entry display name, user name or email address. Omit to skip text filtering.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Name of an entry field to sort by, such as name. The match ignores case. Results are also sorted by name after this field. An unrecognized field name falls back to sorting by name only, and none turns sorting off. The default is name.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. The default is false.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Number of entries to skip, used for paging. The default is 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: Maximum number of entries to return. The default is 100.

200.description: An object with a data array of candidate entries and recordsTotal, the total number of matching entries.

get.summary: List users with explicit console administrator access
get.description:
Returns the users who have been given administrator access to the console directly, rather than through a group.

Permission required: Administrator role or an application (API) token.

200.description: An array of user records.

delete.summary: Remove console administrator access from a user
delete.description:
Removes explicit console administrator access from the specified user. Use it to revoke access that was granted to the user directly.

Permission required: Administrator role or an application (API) token.

Caution: The change takes effect immediately; the user loses console administrator access unless a group or collection they belong to still grants it.

parameters.name: managedAccountId
parameters.description: ID of the user's managed account.

200.description: Access was removed, or the user had no explicit access. The response has no body.

404.description: No user exists with the supplied ID.

put.summary: Give a user console administrator access
put.description:
Grants administrator access to the console to the specified user. The call takes no request body.

Permission required: Administrator role or an application (API) token.

Caution: The change takes effect immediately and grants the user console administrator access.

parameters.name: managedAccountId
parameters.description: ID of the user's managed account.

200.description: Access was granted, or the entry already had it. The response has no body.

404.description: No user exists with the supplied ID.

get.summary: List credentials of one type
get.description:
Returns the credentials of one type. Without a type it returns the Configuration credentials, which are the service accounts used by resources. The Search route is the better choice for most uses.

Permission required: Admin or App role, or the UserPlus role with the Credentials permission.

Values for `CredentialType`: -1 = Any, 0 = Configuration, 1 = User, 2 = Service, 3 = ActivityToken, 4 = Application, 5 = VaultUser, 6 = SshKeyCert.

Caution: The response lists credential details and can include deleted credentials unless includeDeleted is false.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The credential type to return, as a number. The default is 0 (Configuration). Use -1 to return every type.

parameters.name: userName
parameters.description: Returns only credentials whose user name matches this value exactly, ignoring case. Accepts DOMAIN\user or user@domain; without a domain, only credentials with no domain match. When you set userName, includeDeleted is ignored and the list is not sorted.

parameters.name: includeDeleted
parameters.description: Set to false to leave out deleted credentials. The default is true. Without userName, results are sorted by name, domain and user name.

200.description: A list of credentials. Password, enable password, key and passphrase fields are left out.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role or permission.

post.description:
Creates a credential (service account) that NPS uses to sign in to resources. If the request carries the ID of an existing credential and a domain, that credential is updated instead and set to the Configuration type. If the domain and user name already belong to a different credential, the call returns 409.

Permission required: Admin role.

Values for `AuthenticationMethodType`: 0 = Password, 1 = SshCertificate, 2 = SshCertificateAndPassword.

Values for `CredentialType`: -1 = Any, 0 = Configuration, 1 = User, 2 = Service, 3 = ActivityToken, 4 = Application, 5 = VaultUser, 6 = SshKeyCert.

Caution: The request body contains the account password or private key, so send it only over a secure connection and do not log it.

requestBody.description:
The credential to create.

- `id` (string (GUID)): The credential ID. Leave empty for a new credential.
- `name` (string): The display name of the service account.
- `description` (string): A description of the credential.
- `platformId` (string (GUID)): The ID of the platform the account belongs to.
- `username` (string, required): The user name. The request fails if it is empty. A DOMAIN\user or user@domain value is split into domain and user name.
- `password` (string): The password. Required unless you give a private key or a password vault connector. Stored encrypted.
- `enablePassword` (string): The enable password, used by some network devices. Stored encrypted.
- `domain` (string): The domain, for a domain account.
- `type` (integer): The credential type. A number; see the `Values for` paragraphs in the operation description.
- `authenticationMethod` (integer): How the credential authenticates. A number; see the `Values for AuthenticationMethodType` paragraph in the operation description. Use privateKey with the SSH certificate methods.
- `privateKey` (string): The SSH private key. Stored encrypted.
- `passphrase` (string): The passphrase for the private key. Stored encrypted.
- `publicKey` (string): The SSH public key. Stored encrypted.
- `passwordVaultConnectorId` (string (GUID)): The ID of a password vault connector that holds the password.

200.description: The credential. Password, enable password, key and passphrase fields are left out.

400.description: The user name is missing, no password, private key or password vault connector was given, the user name and domain match an existing NPS user, or saving failed. When the request updates an existing credential, an SSH key that is not valid also returns 400. The body describes the problem.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

409.description: The domain and user name already belong to a different service account.

get.summary: Count credentials
get.description:
Returns a single number: how many credentials and discovered users match, using the same set as the Search route (Application-type credentials are not counted). For users with the UserPlus role the count covers only the items that user can see.

Permission required: Admin role, or the UserPlus role with the Credentials permission.

parameters.name: includeDeleted
parameters.description: Set to true to include deleted credentials in the count. The default is false.

200.description: The number of credentials.

400.description: The count could not be read. The body describes the problem.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role or permission.

post.description:
Marks the credentials whose IDs you list as deleted and reports how many were deleted and how many failed. An ID that does not match a credential counts as a failure. Unlike the single delete route, it does not check whether a domain or resource still uses the credential. Use it to remove many credentials in one call.

Permission required: Admin role.

Caution: The listed credentials are marked deleted immediately.

requestBody.description:
A JSON array of credential IDs to delete.

- `(array item)` (string (GUID), required): The ID of one credential to delete. The body is a bare array of IDs.

200.description: Two counts: the number of credentials deleted and the number that failed.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

get.summary: List credential authentication methods
get.description:
Returns the authentication methods a credential can use, as names with their numbers. Use it to look up the values for the authenticationMethod field.

Permission required: Admin or App role.

Values for `AuthenticationMethodType`: 0 = Password, 1 = SshCertificate, 2 = SshCertificateAndPassword.

200.description: An object that maps each method name to its number.

schema.description: Each authentication method name with its number.

400.description: The list could not be read.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

get.summary: Get the SSH key for a credential
get.description:
Returns the SSH key settings for one SSH key credential, including the private key, public key and passphrase in plain text. Use it when you need to retrieve the key material.

Permission required: Admin or App role.

Values for `AuthenticationMethodType`: 0 = Password, 1 = SshCertificate, 2 = SshCertificateAndPassword.

Values for `CredentialType`: -1 = Any, 0 = Configuration, 1 = User, 2 = Service, 3 = ActivityToken, 4 = Application, 5 = VaultUser, 6 = SshKeyCert.

Caution: The response contains the private key and passphrase in plain text, so protect it and do not log it.

parameters.name: credentialId
parameters.description: The ID of the credential.

200.description: The body wraps the key settings: value holds the credential ID, type, authentication method, key settings, private key, passphrase, public key and sudo command, and statusCode is 200. The other wrapper properties are empty.

400.description: The key could not be read. The body describes the problem.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: No credential of the SSH key type exists with that ID.

get.summary: List credential types
get.description:
Returns the credential types as names with their numbers. Use it to look up the values for the type field and the type and credentialType query parameters.

Permission required: Admin or App role.

Values for `CredentialType`: -1 = Any, 0 = Configuration, 1 = User, 2 = Service, 3 = ActivityToken, 4 = Application, 5 = VaultUser, 6 = SshKeyCert.

200.description: An object that maps each credential type name to its number.

schema.description: Each credential type name with its number.

400.description: The list could not be read.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

put.description:
Sets whether the passwords of the listed credentials change at the start of a session, at the end of a session, or both, and what happens to the account afterward. It applies only to credentials whose managed user rotates automatically. The credentials are updated in list order, so if one fails, the ones before it are already changed.

Permission required: Admin or App role.

Values for `PostSessionAction`: 0 = Disable, 1 = Enable, 2 = KeepPrevious.

parameters.name: changeOnCheckout
parameters.description: Set to true to change the password when a session starts. Defaults to false when omitted.

parameters.name: changeOnRelease
parameters.description: Set to true to change the password when a session ends. Defaults to false when omitted.

parameters.name: postSessionAction
parameters.description: What happens to the account after the session ends, as a number. Defaults to 0 (Disable) when omitted.

requestBody.description:
A JSON array of credential IDs to update.

- `(array item)` (string (GUID), required): The ID of one credential. The list cannot be empty. Every credential must have an automatically rotated managed user.

202.description: The settings were accepted and applied.

400.description: The list was empty, an ID was empty, a managed user is not automatic, or the update failed.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: A credential or its managed user was not found.

get.summary: Search credentials and discovered users
get.description:
Returns one page of credentials and discovered users, including users found by directory sync and host scans. You can filter by text, type, management state and privilege. Application-type credentials are never returned, and credentials held in a password vault are left out unless the deployment is set to release them. For users with only the UserPlus role, the results cover only what that user can see.

Permission required: Admin or App role, or the UserPlus role with the Credentials permission.

Values for `ManagedType (managedType)`: -1 = All, 0 = Internal, 1 = Standard, 2 = Service.

Values for `CredentialType`: -1 = Any, 0 = Configuration, 1 = User, 2 = Service, 3 = ActivityToken, 4 = Application, 5 = VaultUser, 6 = SshKeyCert.

Values for `CredentialSearchManagedFilter (managedFilter)`: -1 = All, 0 = NotManaged, 1 = Managed, 2 = Automatic, 3 = Manual.

Values for `UserPrivilege (privilegeFilter)`: 0 = NotSet, 1 = Administrator, 2 = PowerUser, 3 = Guest, 4 = User, 5 = SuperUser, 6 = LinuxUser, 7 = CiscoPrivilege_0, 8 = CiscoPrivilege_1, 9 = CiscoPrivilege_2, 10 = CiscoPrivilege_3, 11 = CiscoPrivilege_4, 12 = CiscoPrivilege_5, 13 = CiscoPrivilege_6, 14 = CiscoPrivilege_7, 15 = CiscoPrivilege_8, 16 = CiscoPrivilege_9, 17 = CiscoPrivilege_10, 18 = CiscoPrivilege_11, 19 = CiscoPrivilege_12, 20 = CiscoPrivilege_13, 21 = CiscoPrivilege_14, 22 = CiscoPrivilege_15, 23 = DomainAdmin, 24 = EnterpriseAdmin.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Returns only items where this text appears, ignoring case, in the user name, platform, domain or privilege name.

parameters.name: managedType
parameters.description: Limits results by account kind. A number; the default is -1 (All).

parameters.name: credentialType
parameters.description: Limits results to one credential type. A number; the default is -1 (Any). Application (4) credentials are never returned, so that value returns nothing.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The number of items to skip. The default is 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: The number of items to return. The default is 10.

parameters.name: includeDeleted
parameters.description: Set to true to include deleted items. The default is false.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: The name of the property to sort by.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. The default is false.

parameters.name: managedFilter
parameters.description: Limits results by management state. A number; the default is -1 (All).

parameters.name: privilegeFilter
parameters.description: Limits results to one privilege level, as a number. When omitted, privilege is not filtered.

200.description: An object with the page of results in data and the total number of matches in recordsTotal.

400.description: The search failed. The body describes the problem.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role or permission.

get.summary: List supported SSH key algorithms
get.description:
Returns the SSH key algorithms the product supports (RSA and ECDSA). Each algorithm lists the key lengths it allows: 1024, 2048 and 4096 for RSA, and 256, 384 and 521 for ECDSA. Use it to choose values for keyGenAlgorithm and keyLength.

Permission required: Admin or App role.

200.description: An object that maps each algorithm name to a list of supported key lengths.

400.description: The list could not be read.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

delete.description:
Deletes one credential (service account) by ID. The credential is marked deleted and removed from any access policies it belongs to. Use it to remove a credential that is no longer needed.

Permission required: Admin or App role.

Caution: The change takes effect immediately and removes the credential from any access policies it belongs to.

parameters.name: credentialId
parameters.description: The ID of the credential.

200.description: The credential was deleted.

400.description: The credential was not found (the body is empty), or it cannot be deleted because a domain or a resource with no other credential to fall back on still uses it (the body describes the problem).

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

get.summary: Get a credential by ID
get.description:
Returns one credential, including whether it is managed. Password, key and passphrase values are blank unless you set showPassword to true. For Admin users, showPassword has no effect on Configuration (service account) credentials, and each password view by an Admin is recorded as an event.

Permission required: Admin or App role, or the UserPlus role with the Credentials permission.

Values for `CredentialType`: -1 = Any, 0 = Configuration, 1 = User, 2 = Service, 3 = ActivityToken, 4 = Application, 5 = VaultUser, 6 = SshKeyCert.

Values for `AuthenticationMethodType`: 0 = Password, 1 = SshCertificate, 2 = SshCertificateAndPassword.

Caution: With showPassword set to true the response contains secrets in plain text, and a password view by an Admin is recorded as an event and forwarded to any configured SIEM.

parameters.name: credentialId
parameters.description: The ID of the credential.

parameters.name: showPassword
parameters.description: Set to true to include the password, keys and passphrase in plain text. The default is false.

200.description: The credential, with an isManaged flag and its comment.

400.description: The credential ID was empty.

401.description: The built-in Administrator account asked to view the current password, which it cannot do.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role or permission.

404.description: No credential exists with that ID.

put.description:
Replaces the settings of one credential with the body you send. A blank password or enable password keeps the stored value, so you can update other fields without re-sending secrets.

Permission required: Admin, App or UserPlus role. A UserPlus user also needs the Credential Manage permission for this credential.

Values for `AuthenticationMethodType`: 0 = Password, 1 = SshCertificate, 2 = SshCertificateAndPassword.

Values for `CredentialType`: -1 = Any, 0 = Configuration, 1 = User, 2 = Service, 3 = ActivityToken, 4 = Application, 5 = VaultUser, 6 = SshKeyCert.

Caution: The change takes effect immediately, and the request body can contain secrets, so send it only over a secure connection.

parameters.name: credentialId
parameters.description: The ID of the credential. It must match the id in the body.

requestBody.description:
The full credential with your changes.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): The credential ID. Must match the id in the URL.
- `name` (string): The display name.
- `description` (string): A description of the credential.
- `username` (string): The user name. A DOMAIN\user or user@domain value is split into domain and user name.
- `domain` (string): The domain, for a domain account.
- `password` (string): The new password. Leave blank to keep the stored password. Stored encrypted.
- `enablePassword` (string): The new enable password. Leave blank to keep the stored value. Stored encrypted.
- `type` (integer): The credential type. A number; see the `Values for` paragraphs in the operation description.
- `authenticationMethod` (integer): How the credential authenticates. A number; see the `Values for AuthenticationMethodType` paragraph in the operation description.
- `privateKey` (string): The SSH private key. Used with the SSH certificate methods. Leave privateKey and passphrase blank to keep the stored key. If you send either, the key is validated.
- `passphrase` (string): The passphrase for the private key. Used with the SSH certificate methods. Leave blank to keep the stored passphrase.
- `publicKey` (string): The SSH public key.
- `passwordVaultConnectorId` (string (GUID)): The ID of a password vault connector that holds the password.

200.description: The updated credential. Password, enable password, key and passphrase fields are left out.

400.description: The id in the body does not match the URL, the user name matches an existing NPS user, or the update failed. The body describes the problem.

401.description: A UserPlus user does not have permission to manage this credential.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

409.description: The domain and user name already belong to another service account.

post.description:
Creates a credential group from the name and description in the request body and returns the new group. Use it to collect credentials so that access policies can refer to them together.

Permission required: Admin role.

requestBody.description:
The credential group to create.

- `name` (string, required): The name of the credential group. Up to 256 characters.
- `description` (string): A description of the group.

200.description: The credential group was created. The body is the new group, including its ID.

400.description: The group could not be created, for example because the body is missing. The body contains the error message.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the Admin role.

post.summary: Add credentials to a credential group
post.description:
Adds the credentials whose IDs are in the request body to the credential group. The response is the number of credentials added.

Permission required: Admin role.

parameters.name: credentialGroupId
parameters.description: The ID of the credential group.

requestBody.description:
An array of credential IDs to add to the group.

- `(array item)` (string (GUID), required): The ID of a credential to add. The body is a JSON array of IDs, not an object.

200.description: The credentials were added. The body is the number added; credentials already in the group are skipped and not counted.

400.description: The group ID is empty or the credentials could not be added. The body contains the error message.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the Admin role.

404.description: No credential group with that ID exists.

get.summary: List credential group names and IDs
get.description:
Returns the name and ID of each credential group. Use it to fill a list or to find a group ID. You can narrow the list with filter text.

Permission required: Admin or App role.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Text to filter the group names by. The default is an empty string, which returns all groups.

200.description: An array of objects, each with the ID and name of a credential group.

400.description: The list could not be retrieved. The body contains the error message.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the Admin or App role.

get.summary: Search the credentials in a credential group
get.description:
Returns a page of the credentials that belong to one credential group. Application credentials are not included. Use it to see the group's members, with optional filtering, sorting and paging.

Permission required: Admin role.

Values for `managedType`: -1 = All, 0 = Internal, 1 = Standard, 2 = Service.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the credential group.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Text to match in the credential display name. The default is an empty string, which applies no filter.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The number of results to skip. The default is 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: The number of results to return. The default is 10.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: The name of the field to sort the results by. If you leave it out, results are sorted by display name.

post.description:
