delete.description:
Removes one or more roles from a group in a single call. The Administrator role cannot be removed from a group that the signed-in administrator belongs to; that item counts as failed. The Administrator role can be removed only from a group that is backed by a directory group; otherwise that item counts as failed. The server reads the list from the request body of this DELETE request, so the body is required. Some HTTP clients and API tools drop the body of a DELETE request; check that yours sends it.

Permission required: Administrator role.

parameters.name: managedAccountGroupId
parameters.description: The ID of the group (managed account group) on the Users & Groups page.

requestBody.description:
A JSON array of the roles to remove. Send each role with its id and name.

- `id` (string (GUID)): The ID of the role. Required for a custom role, which is matched by ID. Not used for the built-in Administrator and Reviewer roles.
- `name` (string): The name of the role. Required for the built-in roles, which are matched by this exact name: Administrator or Reviewer. The console sends it for every role.

200.description: Returns the number of roles removed (passed), the number that failed, and a message for each item.

400.description: The roles could not be removed.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role, or the account has read-only administrator access.

404.description: The group does not exist, or the signed-in user's account could not be found.

get.summary: List the roles of a user
get.description:
Returns the roles that a user holds, as a page of results that you can filter by name or description. The built-in Administrator and Reviewer roles appear when the user has them.

Permission required: Administrator role.

Values for `roleTarget`: 0 = AccessPolicies, 1 = Credentials, 2 = Auditors.

parameters.name: managedAccountId
parameters.description: The ID of the user (managed account) on the Users & Groups page.

parameters.name: Skip
parameters.description: The number of rows to skip, for paging. The default is 0.

parameters.name: Take
parameters.description: The maximum number of rows to return. The default is 100.

parameters.name: OrderBy
parameters.description: A property name of the returned rows, ignoring case. The default is Name. An unrecognized name returns the rows ordered by ID.

parameters.name: OrderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. The default is false.

parameters.name: FilterText
parameters.description: Returns only roles whose name or description contains this value, ignoring case.

parameters.name: FilterColumns
parameters.description: Not used by this route.

200.description: Returns a page of results in data, with the total number of matching rows in recordsTotal.

400.description: The roles could not be retrieved.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The user does not exist.

get.summary: List the roles of a group
get.description:
Returns the roles that a group holds, as a page of results that you can filter by name or description. The built-in Administrator and Reviewer roles appear when the group has them.

Permission required: Administrator role.

Values for `roleTarget`: 0 = AccessPolicies, 1 = Credentials, 2 = Auditors.

parameters.name: managedAccountGroupId
parameters.description: The ID of the group (managed account group) on the Users & Groups page.

parameters.name: Skip
parameters.description: The number of rows to skip, for paging. The default is 0.

parameters.name: Take
parameters.description: The maximum number of rows to return. The default is 100.

parameters.name: OrderBy
parameters.description: A property name of the returned rows, ignoring case. The default is Name. An unrecognized name returns the rows ordered by ID.

parameters.name: OrderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort in descending order. The default is false.

parameters.name: FilterText
parameters.description: Returns only roles whose name or description contains this value, ignoring case.

parameters.name: FilterColumns
parameters.description: Not used by this route.

200.description: Returns a page of results in data, with the total number of matching rows in recordsTotal.

400.description: The roles could not be retrieved.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

404.description: The group does not exist.

delete.description:
Deletes a role. The role no longer appears in role lists, and its members no longer receive the permissions it granted. Use it when a delegated responsibility is no longer needed.

Permission required: Administrator role.

Caution: The role is deleted immediately and its members lose the access it granted.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: The ID of the role.

200.description: The role was deleted. There is no response body.

400.description: The role could not be deleted.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role, or the account has read-only administrator access.

404.description: The role does not exist.

get.summary: Get a role
get.description:
Returns one role with its name, description, target and the flags that say whether it covers all activities, credentials, policies, resources or users. It does not return the permissions or the members of the role. Use the other role routes for those.

Permission required: Administrator role.

Values for `roleTarget`: 0 = AccessPolicies, 1 = Credentials, 2 = Auditors.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: The ID of the role.

200.description: Returns the role.

400.description: The role could not be retrieved.

403.description: The signed-in user does not have the required role.

put.description:

Fields you leave out are reset to their defaults (false, or 0 for the target), so send the full role. The ID in the body must match the ID in the path. Use it to rename a role or change its description.

Permission required: Administrator role.

Values for `roleTarget`: 0 = AccessPolicies, 1 = Credentials, 2 = Auditors.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: The ID of the role.

post.description:
Adds a SIEM server that receives events. The server assigns the name, so any name you send is ignored.

Permission required: Admin or App role.

Caution: The server is saved immediately and starts receiving events if it is enabled.

parameters.name: test
parameters.description: Set to true to leave the Location header out of the response. The SIEM server is still saved.

requestBody.description:
The SIEM server settings.

- `id` (string (GUID)): The ID of the SIEM server. Ignored on create.
- `host` (string): The host name or address of the SIEM server. Not checked by the server, but needed for events to be delivered.
- `port` (integer): The port the SIEM server listens on. Not checked by the server, but needed for events to be delivered.
- `serverType` (string): The transport used to send events: Udp or Tcp. Case-insensitive text, not a number. Any other value is saved but no events are sent to the server.
- `protocol` (string): The TLS version to use for a TCP connection when useSsl is true. Text: Tls, Tls11, Tls12 or Tls13 (case-insensitive). Empty or any other value means no TLS. Ignored for Udp.
- `useSsl` (boolean): Whether to encrypt the connection. Applies to Tcp servers only, and only takes effect when protocol names a TLS version.
- `enabled` (boolean): Whether events are sent to this server.
- `siemTemplateId` (string (GUID)): The ID of the SIEM template that formats the events.
- `name` (string): The name of the server. Ignored. The server assigns a generated name.

201.description: The SIEM server was created. The body is the saved server, and the Location header points to it unless test is true.

400.description: The SIEM server could not be created.

put.description:
Changes the settings of an existing SIEM server, identified by the id in the body. The server keeps the existing name.

Permission required: Admin or App role.

Caution: The change is saved immediately and affects where events are sent.

requestBody.description:
The full SIEM server settings. Values you send replace the stored ones, so include every field you want to keep.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): The ID of the SIEM server. Identifies the SIEM server to update.
- `host` (string): The host name or address of the SIEM server. Not checked by the server, but needed for events to be delivered.
- `port` (integer): The port the SIEM server listens on. Not checked by the server, but needed for events to be delivered.
- `serverType` (string): The transport used to send events: Udp or Tcp. Case-insensitive text, not a number. Any other value is saved but no events are sent to the server.
- `protocol` (string): The TLS version to use for a TCP connection when useSsl is true. Text: Tls, Tls11, Tls12 or Tls13 (case-insensitive). Empty or any other value means no TLS. Ignored for Udp.
- `useSsl` (boolean): Whether to encrypt the connection. Applies to Tcp servers only, and only takes effect when protocol names a TLS version.
- `enabled` (boolean): Whether events are sent to this server.
- `siemTemplateId` (string (GUID)): The ID of the SIEM template that formats the events.
- `name` (string): The name of the server. Ignored. The existing name is kept.

200.description: The SIEM server was updated. The body is empty.

400.description: The update failed.

post.description:
Creates a SIEM template and returns the saved template. Use it to define the message format that is sent to a SIEM server.

Permission required: Administrator role (or an application account with the App role).

parameters.name: test
parameters.description: Used for testing. When true, the response does not include the URL of the new template. Default is false.

The SIEM template to create.

- `id` (string (uuid)): Omit it; the server generates an ID for the new template. The saved template in the response includes the ID.
- `name` (string): The display name of the template. Must be unique across SIEM templates. Up to 256 characters.
- `description` (string): A description of the template.
- `templateFormat` (string): The layout of the message sent to the SIEM server. Write each attribute in upper case between percent signs, for example %EVENTTIMEUTC%. Get the attribute names from the attributes route. The format also accepts %SYSLOG_DATE%, %HOST%, %TEMPLATENAME%, %TEMPLATEVERSION%, %COMPANY%, %PRODUCT%, %PRODUCT_VERSION%, %LOGLEVEL% and %LOGLEVELSTATUS%, and \t for a tab.
- `version` (string): A version label for the template. Used for %TEMPLATEVERSION%; when empty, 1.0 is used.
- `charactersToEscape` (string): Each character in this string is escaped in the formatted message.
- `escapeCharacter` (string): The text placed before each escaped character.
- `nodeId` (string (uuid)): Internal value set by the server. Do not send it. On update the stored value is always kept.
- `createdDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Set by the server; any value you send is replaced.
- `modifiedDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Set by the server; any value you send is replaced.

201.description: The template was created. The body contains the saved template.

400.description: The template could not be created, for example because another template has the same name. The response body contains the error message.

put.description:
Replaces the settings of an existing SIEM template. The id in the request body identifies the template; send every field, because fields you leave out are cleared.

Permission required: Administrator role (or an application account with the App role).

requestBody.description:
The full SIEM template. Fields you leave out are cleared.

- `id` (string (uuid), required): The ID of the template to update.
- `name` (string): The display name of the template. Must be unique across SIEM templates. Up to 256 characters.
- `description` (string): A description of the template.
- `templateFormat` (string): The layout of the message sent to the SIEM server. Write each attribute in upper case between percent signs, for example %EVENTTIMEUTC%. Get the attribute names from the attributes route. The format also accepts %SYSLOG_DATE%, %HOST%, %TEMPLATENAME%, %TEMPLATEVERSION%, %COMPANY%, %PRODUCT%, %PRODUCT_VERSION%, %LOGLEVEL% and %LOGLEVELSTATUS%, and \t for a tab.
- `version` (string): A version label for the template. Used for %TEMPLATEVERSION%; when empty, 1.0 is used.
- `charactersToEscape` (string): Each character in this string is escaped in the formatted message.
- `escapeCharacter` (string): The text placed before each escaped character.
- `nodeId` (string (uuid)): Internal value set by the server. Do not send it. On update the stored value is always kept.
- `createdDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Omit it to keep the stored creation time.
- `modifiedDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Set by the server; any value you send is replaced.

200.description: The template was updated. The response body is empty.

400.description: The template could not be updated. The response body contains the error message.

get.summary: Get the idle user period

Returns the number of days without sign-in after which Privilege Secure removes a user's account. A value of 0 means the check is off. Application users and console access members are not removed.

This route does not require a sign-in.

400.description: The setting could not be read.

The idle user setting to save.

200.description: Returns the saved value.

400.description: The value is not 0 or between 90 and 365, or the setting could not be saved.

get.summary: Get RDP file options
get.description:
Returns the settings Privilege Secure uses when it builds RDP files: the default and allowed resolutions, multi-monitor, smart sizing and the certificate used to sign the file.

Permission required: Admin or App role.

200.description: Returns the RDP file options.

400.description: The options could not be retrieved.

404.description: No RDP file options exist.

post.description:
Sets the default and allowed resolutions, multi-monitor, smart sizing and signing certificate that Privilege Secure uses when it builds RDP files. Returns the saved options.

Permission required: Admin or App role.

requestBody.description:
The RDP file options to save. Send back the object returned by the GET route with your changes.

- `defaultResolution` (string): Resolution used by default for RDP sessions. If left out, the stored value is replaced with null.
- `allowedResolutions` (array of string, required): Resolutions a user can choose. Required; null returns 400. Saved as a comma-separated list.
- `multiMonitor` (boolean): Whether RDP sessions can use multiple monitors. If left out, false is saved.
- `smartSizing` (boolean): Whether RDP sessions scale to fit the window. If left out, false is saved.
- `certificateThumbprint` (string): Thumbprint of the certificate used to sign RDP files. Use the Certificates route to find one. May be null for no certificate.
- `id` (string (GUID), required): ID of the options record. Required. Use the value returned by the GET route; an unknown or missing ID returns 400.

- `createdDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Set by the server. Leave as returned. Ignored; not saved. Leave as returned.
- `modifiedDateTimeUtc` (string (date-time)): Set by the server. Leave as returned. Ignored; not saved. Leave as returned.

200.description: Returns the saved options.

400.description: The ID is unknown, allowedResolutions is missing, or the options could not be saved.

404.description: The options could not be saved because no record was returned.

get.summary: Get the console idle timeout
get.description:

put.description:

200.description: Returns the saved timeout.

400.description: The value is out of range, the body is missing, or the setting could not be saved.

get.summary: Get WinRM connection settings
get.description:
Returns whether Privilege Secure connects to Windows computers over WinRM using HTTP or HTTPS, and the thumbprint of the certificate it uses.

The WinRM settings to save.

put.description:

get.description:

post.summary: Create a user and group collection
post.description:

Adds a URL rule that tells the system which pages belong to a website.

Permission required: Admin role.

Values for `matchType`: -1 = All, 0 = Domain, 1 = Exact, 2 = Never, 3 = StartsWith, 4 = Regex, 5 = Host.

Values for `match`: -1 = All, 0 = Domain, 1 = Exact, 2 = Never, 3 = StartsWith, 4 = Regex, 5 = Host.

requestBody.description:
The URL rule to add.

- `id` (string (GUID)): The ID of the URL rule. Leave empty when creating.
- `websiteId` (string (GUID), required): The ID of the website the rule belongs to. Required.
- `uri` (string, required): The address or pattern to match. Required.
- `match` (integer): An older field for how the address is matched. Set it to the same value as matchType.
- `matchType` (integer): How the address is matched. The URL rule search filters on this field. 0 = Domain, 1 = Exact, 2 = Never, 3 = StartsWith, 4 = Regex, 5 = Host. Do not use -1 (All), which is only a search filter value.
- `nodeId` (string (GUID)): Internal server ID. Do not send. Set by the server.

200.description: The body is the created URL rule.

400.description: The rule could not be created.

put.description:
Updates an existing URL rule of a website. Send the full rule, including its ID.

Permission required: Admin role.

Values for `matchType`: -1 = All, 0 = Domain, 1 = Exact, 2 = Never, 3 = StartsWith, 4 = Regex, 5 = Host.

Values for `match`: -1 = All, 0 = Domain, 1 = Exact, 2 = Never, 3 = StartsWith, 4 = Regex, 5 = Host.

requestBody.description:
The URL rule with its changes.

- `id` (string (GUID), required): The ID of the URL rule. Required. Identifies the rule to update.
- `websiteId` (string (GUID), required): The ID of the website the rule belongs to. Required.
- `uri` (string, required): The address or pattern to match. Required.
- `match` (integer): An older field for how the address is matched. Set it to the same value as matchType.
- `matchType` (integer): How the address is matched. The URL rule search filters on this field. 0 = Domain, 1 = Exact, 2 = Never, 3 = StartsWith, 4 = Regex, 5 = Host. Do not use -1 (All), which is only a search filter value.
- `nodeId` (string (GUID)): Internal server ID. Do not send. Set by the server.

200.description: The body is the updated URL rule.

400.description: The rule could not be updated.

post.description:
Deletes several URL rules in one call. The IDs are processed in order.

Permission required: Admin role.

Caution: If one ID cannot be deleted, the call stops and returns 400; the IDs before it stay deleted.

requestBody.description:
A JSON array of URL rule IDs to delete.

- `(body)` (array of string (GUID), required): The IDs of the rules to delete.

200.description: The rules were deleted. The body is a confirmation message.

400.description: One of the rules could not be deleted. Rules earlier in the list were already deleted.

get.summary: Search the URL rules of a website
get.description:
Returns a page of the URL rules that identify pages of one website, optionally filtered by match type and by text contained in the rule's address.

Permission required: Admin role.

Values for `matchType`: -1 = All, 0 = Domain, 1 = Exact, 2 = Never, 3 = StartsWith, 4 = Regex, 5 = Host.

parameters.name: websiteId
parameters.description: The ID of the website.

parameters.name: filterType
parameters.description: Only return rules with this match type (the matchType field). The default is -1 (all).

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Only return rules whose address contains this text (not case-sensitive).

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: The name of the field to sort by.

parameters.name: orderDescending
parameters.description: Set to true to sort from highest to lowest. The default is false.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: The number of results to skip. The default is 0.

parameters.name: take
parameters.description: The maximum number of results to return. The default is 100.

200.description: The body is a page of URL rules with the total count.

400.description: The website ID is empty or the search failed.

get.summary: Get a website URL rule
get.description:
Returns one URL rule of a website by its ID, including its address, match type and timestamps.

Permission required: Any signed-in user.

Values for `matchType`: -1 = All, 0 = Domain, 1 = Exact, 2 = Never, 3 = StartsWith, 4 = Regex, 5 = Host.

Values for `match`: -1 = All, 0 = Domain, 1 = Exact, 2 = Never, 3 = StartsWith, 4 = Regex, 5 = Host.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the URL rule.

200.description: The body is the URL rule.

204.description: No rule has that ID. The body is empty.

400.description: The rule could not be retrieved.

post.summary: Sign in with a form post and get a token
post.description:
Checks a user name and password sent as form fields and returns a token. If the user must give a multi-factor code, send the returned token to the sign-in verification route to finish. This route is outside the /api/v1 path.

Permission required: No sign-in required.

Caution: The request carries a password and the response carries a token that grants access as the user; use HTTPS and store the token securely.

login.description: The user name to sign in with. Local user name or DOMAIN\user.
The user name to sign in with. Local user name or DOMAIN\user.

requestBody.description:
The credentials, sent as form fields (application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart/form-data).

- `login` (string, required): The user name to sign in with. Local user name or DOMAIN\user.
- `password` (string, required): The password for the user. Sensitive value.

200.description: The body is the token as a string.

400.description: The user is not allowed to sign in with a password, or licensing blocks sign-in. The body is a message.

401.description: Credentials are wrong or empty, the database could not be reached, or an unexpected error occurred. The body is a message.

post.summary: Complete sign-in with a multi-factor code
post.description:
Finishes a sign-in that requires multi-factor authentication. Send the token from the first sign-in step as a Bearer token and the code as a JSON string; the response is the session token. This route is outside the /api/v1 path.

Permission required: A first-step sign-in token (password accepted, multi-factor code pending).

Caution: The response contains a session token that grants access as the user; store it securely.

parameters.name: extension
parameters.description: Set to true when the sign-in is for a browser extension. The default is false.

requestBody.description:
The multi-factor code as a raw JSON string, for example "123456".

- `(body)` (string, required): The code from the user's authenticator or multi-factor provider. If the account uses the built-in Multi-factor Not Required connector, any value is accepted.

200.description: The body is the session token as a JSON string. If the sign-in session cannot be found (for example, browser cookies are blocked), the status is still 200 but the body is a JSON object with an error message instead of a token.

401.description: The code is not valid or was used recently, two-factor is not enabled for the user, or the multi-factor provider rejected it. The body is a message.

post.summary: Sign in with a JSON body and get a token
post.description:
Checks a user name and password sent as JSON and returns a token. If the user must give a multi-factor code, send the returned token to the sign-in verification route to finish. This route is outside the /api/v1 path.

Permission required: No sign-in required.

Caution: The request carries a password and the response carries a token that grants access as the user; use HTTPS and store the token securely.

requestBody.description:
The credentials as a JSON object.

- `login` (string, required): The user name to sign in with. Local user name or DOMAIN\user.
- `password` (string, required): The password for the user. Sensitive value.

200.description: The body is the token as a JSON string.

400.description: The user is not allowed to sign in with a password, or licensing blocks sign-in. The body is a message.

401.description: Credentials are wrong or empty, the database could not be reached, or an unexpected error occurred. The body is a message.

bearerAuth.description: JSON Web Token returned by the sign-in call.
